# EPURE — Complete Documentation Corpus (EN + FR + Glossary)

---
## [EN] Introduction & Naming (L'Épure)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/introduction

# Introduction & The Meaning of EPURE

**EPURE** (`Giskard-AI/epure`) is a GitHub-first, specification-driven software engineering framework that combines **structured human architectural governance** with **autonomous multi-agent TDD implementation and code review**.

**EPURE** brings a deterministic specification lock (`spec_sha`), a single declarative repository configuration (`.github/agents.yml`), and a reproducible issue-to-release workflow to AI-assisted software engineering.

---

## Why the Name "EPURE"?

The name **EPURE** carries a dual meaning rooted in French architectural heritage and modern software engineering:

### 1. The Architectural Blueprint (*L'Épure d'Architecte*)

In classical French architecture, stonecutting (*stéréotomie*), and naval carpentry, **une épure** is the full-scale geometrical working drawing traced on a workshop wall or floor before a single block of stone is cut or a beam is shaped.

In software engineering with AI agents, the most common failure mode is **premature coding**: letting an LLM guess product requirements, invent domain vocabulary, or silently choose trade-offs inside a pull request. EPURE enforces the exact opposite discipline:

1. **Draw the blueprint first**: On a GitHub tracking issue, the maintainer and the agent clarify every ambiguity through a structured interview (**Grill**).
2. **Version the domain and specification**: Before any application code is written, EPURE commits the ubiquitous language (`GLOSSARY.md`), Architectural Decision Records (`docs/adr/`), the functional & technical specification (`docs/specs/<slug>.md`), and—when a user interface is involved—the visual design contract (`DESIGN.md`) onto a dedicated `plan/<issue>-<slug>` branch.
3. **Machine the parts under a locked mandate**: Only after a human maintainer signs the blueprint with `/epure approve` (locking the exact `spec_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`) do agents execute the dependency-ordered ticket DAG (`task/* -> feature/*`).

### 2. The Bilingual Acronym

**EPURE** also stands for the four pillars of its execution engine:

| Letter | English Acronym | French Acronym | Engineering Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E** | **Engineered** | **Élaboration** | Structured design interview (`/epure plan` & Grill) that surfaces trade-offs before coding. |
| **P** | **Planning** | **Plans** | Versioned `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, Specification, and dependency-ordered ticket DAG (`blocked_by`). |
| **U** | **Unified** | **Usinage** | Secretless TDD implementation loop (`npm test`, `npm run build`, contract checks) on isolated `task/*` branches. |
| **R** | **Review** | **Revue** | Multi-agent specialist code review loaded from trusted `dev`, Impeccable WCAG AA UI gate, and AI semantic squash. |
| **E** | **Execution** | **Exécution** | Governed integration (`feature/* -> dev` human merge) and fast-forward release promotion (`dev -> main`). |

---

## The Three-Tier Step Taxonomy (Q101)

A core principle of EPURE is transparency about **who decides** and **what runs automatically**. Every step in an EPURE workflow belongs to one of three formal categories:

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-issue-flow"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Global Issue & PR Flow (Human Gates, Mandatory & Conditional Steps)"
  caption="The complete EPURE workflow separated into Mandatory Human Gates, Mandatory Automated Pipeline, Conditional UI Gate, and Optional Controls."
/>

### 1. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Validation Gates (4)</span>

No agent can ever bypass these four decision points. They require an explicit action from a repository contributor with `write` or `admin` permission:

1. **Gate 1 — Initiate & Answer the Grill (`/epure plan`)**: A maintainer triggers `/epure plan` on a GitHub Issue and answers the clarifying questions until the design frontier is settled.
2. **Gate 2 — Sign the Implementation Mandate (`/epure approve`)**: After reviewing the generated spec and ticket DAG on `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, a maintainer comments `/epure approve`. This directly integrates the `plan/*` artifacts into `feature/<issue>-<slug>` (with additive `GLOSSARY.md` merging and monotonic ADR renumbering, without an intermediate `plan/* -> dev` PR per ADR-0031), locks `spec_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, and begins executing the ticket DAG.
3. **Gate 3 — Human Integration Merge (`feature/* -> dev`)**: Once all tickets in the DAG are implemented, reviewed, and squashed into `feature/*` (and verified by `EpicConvergenceAudit`), EPURE opens the final synthesis PR `feature/* -> dev`. The `epure-dev-governance` ruleset **blocks** the Agent App from merging application code into `dev`: a human maintainer must click **Squash and merge**.
4. **Gate 4 — Human Release Promotion (`dev -> main`)**: Promoting `dev` to `main` and publishing a `vX.Y.Z` tag requires a human to trigger the `release-promote.yml` workflow (`workflow_dispatch`).

### 2. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Steps</span>

Once a human gate is crossed, EPURE executes these steps deterministically on every feature:

- **Blueprint, Goldfish Spec Audit & Ticket DAG Generation**: Runs the zero-context Goldfish specification audit (`runGoldfishSpecAudit`), commits `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` (with `EpicGoalContract`) on `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, and creates GitHub Issues for each atomic task with native `sub_issues` and `blocked_by` dependencies and the `ready-for-agent` label.
- **Secretless Kernel Sandbox TDD Loop**: For each unblocked ticket, applies incremental mutations (`write_repo_file`, `patch_repo_file`, `delete_repo_file`) and runs Stage 1 verification inside an isolated 2-phase Linux kernel sandbox (`landrun` / `bubblewrap`) stripped of `LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys.
- **Event-Driven External CI, Trusted `dev` Multi-Agent Review & AI Semantic Squash**: Exits immediately while external CI runs (`waiting_ticket_ci`), resumes on `check_suite.completed` / `workflow_run.completed`, runs up to 4 domain-specialized reviewers (loaded strictly from `dev`) plus `spec-parity-reviewer`, and squash-merges `task/* -> feature/*` with a synthesized Conventional Commit title/body (`Refs #<ticket>`).
- **Zero-Context `EpicConvergenceAudit` & Final Synthesis PR Review**: Runs `runEpicConvergenceAudit` on `feature/*` to ensure all `required_entrypoints` are wired and no `forbidden_stubs` remain (spawning Phase 2 convergence tickets if needed), then opens and audits the consolidated synthesis PR `feature/* -> dev` with `Closes #<issue>` and `Closes #<ticket>` trailer links.

### 3. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional or Conditional Steps</span>

These steps run only when triggered by the nature of the change or by an explicit maintainer command:

- **Conditional UI & Impeccable Gate (automatic when UI exists)**: When the feature or diff touches frontend/UI files (`.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.css`, `.html`), EPURE automatically generates `DESIGN.md`, runs `user-advocate` in `design-gate` mode before `/epure approve`, and enforces `user-advocate` (`implementation-review`) + `impeccable-gate` as blocking checks on every PR. Pure backend/CLI changes skip these steps automatically.
- **Optional Exploratory Prototype (`/prototype` & Isolated Pages Preview)**: When a layout or state interaction cannot be settled in prose during the Grill, a maintainer can request a throwaway prototype on `prototype/*`. Static GitHub Pages preview is **disabled by default** (`enable_pages_preview: false`) and requires explicit opt-in.
- **Optional Granular Slash Commands**:
  - `/epure to-spec`: Validate the Grill frontier (or force early transition) to generate the specification on `plan/*`.
  - `/epure to-tickets`: Validate the specification on `plan/*` and generate the native GitHub ticket DAG (`sub_issues` + `blocked_by`).
  - `/epure continue`: Resume orchestration after a `needs-human` pause, manual fix, or external CI completion (`waiting_ticket_ci` / `waiting_feature_ci`).
  - `/epure sync` (alias `/epure rebase`): Synchronize `dev -> feature/*` (and `feature/* -> task/*`) with 3-way conflict resolution and Stage 1 sandbox verification.
  - `/epure status`: Refresh and post the current orchestration state and ticket table.
  - `/epure cancel` (alias `/epure stop`): Immediately halt orchestration and mark the mandate `cancelled` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`.
- **Conditional Human Escalation (`needs-human`)**: Triggered automatically if a `task/*` branch touches sensitive paths (`.github/workflows/**`, `.github/agents.yml`, the reviewer roster directory `reviewers_dir/**` (default `.agents/reviewers/**`), `CODEOWNERS`) without an approved exception, or if a ticket still fails after `max_code_fix_attempts = 3` remediation rounds.

---

## [EN] Installation & /setup-repo Skill
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/installation

# Installation & Bootstrap

The recommended way to initialize or reconfigure a repository with EPURE is to invoke the **`/setup-repo` agent skill** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`) directly inside your Skills-compatible coding agent.

The `/setup-repo` skill orchestrates the entire bootstrap end-to-end: it inspects your repository's actual architecture, walks you through the interactive wizard (`setup-github-apps-wizard.sh`) to register your two GitHub Apps and isolated GitHub Environments (`<llm-env>` and `release`), runs the deterministic CLI (`dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs`) in `--dry-run` simulation mode before `--apply`, and **dynamically designs your multi-agent reviewer roster (`reviewers_dir`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`)**.

---

## System Requirements

Before bootstrapping a repository with EPURE, ensure your local environment has:

- **A Skills-compatible coding agent** (any IDE or CLI agent that can load `.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`)
- **Node.js 24 LTS** (`>=24.0.0`)
- **GitHub CLI (`gh`)** authenticated against your target GitHub account or organization (`gh auth status`)
- **Git** (`>=2.38`)
- **An LLM API Key** (`LLM_API_KEY` or custom provider key configured in `.github/agents.yml`)

---

## Recommended Way: Bootstrap via the `/setup-repo` Skill

Open your target repository in your coding agent and invoke the **`/setup-repo`** skill:

```text
/setup-repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

The agent executes a guided **4-step workflow** with explicit human confirmation before any sensitive action:

### Step 1: Agent Inspection of Stack & Domain Elements

Before writing any file, the agent inspects the target repository (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`, `src/` directory layout, UI presence, existing `GLOSSARY.md`) to determine:

- The language and build stack to configure `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `verification.targets`, `renovate.json`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, and `standards-reviewer.md`.
- Whether the repository includes a frontend/UI surface (which determines whether the **Impeccable** gate and `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, and `design-reviewer` are included).
- Which domain subsystems warrant creating **custom specialist reviewers** in `.agents/reviewers/<domain>-reviewer.md` (or your configured `reviewers_dir`).

### Step 2: Provision the Two GitHub Apps & Environment-Scoped Secrets (Wizard)

To enforce strict privilege separation (Q82, Q91) and Zizmor-compliant zero secret exposure to unprivileged PR workflows, EPURE never uses a single all-powerful Personal Access Token or global repository secrets. Instead, every repository uses **two distinct GitHub Apps** and **two isolated GitHub Environments** (`<llm-env>` and `release`):

1. **Agent App (`<owner>-epure-agent`)**: Used by the orchestrator for day-to-day automation (`plan/*`, `task/*`, `feature/*`, Issues, PRs, and Check Runs). It is **never** a Bypass Actor on `dev` or `main`.
2. **Release App (`<owner>-epure-release`)**: Used exclusively by `release-promote.yml` / `release.yml` when a human triggers a fast-forward release from `dev` to `main`. It is the **sole Bypass Actor** on `main` and `v*` tags.

Launch the interactive wizard, which supports **Approach 2** (1-click local GitHub App Manifest Flow) with automatic **Fallback Approach 1** (manual step-by-step guided registration) and injects secrets into their dedicated GitHub Environments via `gh secret set --env` without ever exposing PEM private keys to the LLM:

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --llm-env <llm-env>
```

> **Configurable & LLM-Agnostic `<llm-env>`**: The agent environment name (`<llm-env>`) defaults to `epure-agent` and can be chosen freely (other examples: `llm`, `openai`, `anthropic`, or `gemini`; pass the same value to `setup-repo --llm-env`) and matches `environment: <llm-env>` on the `orchestrate-command` job in `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`.

| Secret Name | GitHub Environment Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | `--env <llm-env>` | API key for the LLM client / proxy sidecar (kept out of `authorize-command` and the code execution sandbox). |
| `EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID` | `--env <llm-env>` | Numeric App ID of `<owner>-epure-agent`. |
| `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | `--env <llm-env>` | PEM private key of `<owner>-epure-agent` (used to mint short-lived installation tokens). |
| `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` | `--env release` | Numeric App ID of `<owner>-epure-release` (bound to the human-approved `release` environment). |
| `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | `--env release` | PEM private key of `<owner>-epure-release` (used only by `release.yml` / `release-promote.yml`). |

Verify the environment-scoped secrets with `gh`:

```bash
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator --env <llm-env>
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator --env release
```

### Step 3: Non-Destructive Simulation (`--dry-run`)

The `/setup-repo` skill first runs the underlying CLI in `--dry-run` mode and presents the complete file, branch, label, and ruleset plan for your approval:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --dry-run
```

### Step 4: Guided Application (`--apply`) & Custom Reviewer Roster Design

Once you confirm the dry-run report, the `/setup-repo` skill applies the repository governance via `--apply --apply-github-settings`, and then creates and tailors the reviewer prompts in `.agents/reviewers/*.md` (or the directory chosen with `--reviewers-dir`) specific to your repository:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --apply \
  --apply-github-settings
```

Then commit and push the generated files (`.github/`, `.agents/reviewers/`, and `renovate.json`) to `dev`:

```bash
git add .github/ .agents/reviewers/ renovate.json
git commit -m "chore(epure): bootstrap repository governance and workflows"
git push origin dev
```

---

## What the `/setup-repo` Skill Configures

1. **Branch Topology (`main` & `dev`)**:
   - Ensures both `main` (immutable release line) and `dev` (active integration branch) exist.
   - Sets **`dev` as the default branch** of the repository so Pull Requests target `dev` by default and `Closes #<issue>` trailers resolve automatically when landing on `dev`.
2. **Canonical Triage Labels**:
   - Creates or updates the 5 canonical labels (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`) plus orchestration labels (`needs-human`, `approved-sensitive-change`).
3. **Declarative Configuration, Hardened Supply-Chain & Thin Caller Workflows**:
   - Generates `.github/agents.yml` (flat canonical schema with auto-discovered `verification.targets`), `.github/zizmor.yml` (static workflow security configuration), and `renovate.json` (with 3-to-14-day quarantine cooldowns).
   - Installs `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`, `.github/workflows/epure-check.yml`, `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (tailored to the detected stack), and `.github/workflows/release.yml`, all pinned to the 40-character commit SHA of `Giskard-AI/epure`.
4. **Dynamic Multi-Agent Reviewer Roster (`reviewers_dir`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`)**:
   - The agent running `/setup-repo` **creates, designs, and adds the appropriate `<reviewers_dir>/<role>-reviewer.md` files as needed** based on the repository's actual elements (further refined during `/epure plan`):
     - **Always-On Core (Cross-Cutting & Persona)**: `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer` (adapted to the detected language: TypeScript, Python, Rust, or Go), and `user-advocate`.
     - **Agent-Designed Stack, Domain & UI Specialists**: `domain-backend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, any custom domain specialists designed by the agent for your subsystems (e.g. `realtime-reviewer.md`, `combat-engine-reviewer.md`, `sql-migration-reviewer.md` with YAML frontmatter `paths:` routing), and — only when the project includes a UI — the frontend/Impeccable trio (`frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`).
     - *Illustrative example on `craft-calculator` (TypeScript + React web app)*: the agent composes a 10-reviewer roster combining the always-on core, `domain-backend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, and the 3 UI/Impeccable reviewers.
5. **Squash-Only Merge Governance & 3 Repository Rulesets**:
   - Configures the repository to allow **Squash merge only** (`allow_squash_merge: true`, `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`).
   - Installs the 3 GitHub Repository Rulesets:
     - `epure-feature-governance` (`refs/heads/feature/*`): `Agent App` in PR bypass for autonomous `task/* -> feature/*` squash-merges once checks pass.
     - `epure-dev-governance` (`refs/heads/dev`): No `Agent App` bypass (`required_approving_review_count: 0` by default for solo-maintainer compatibility; configurable via `--require-pr-approvals <N>`).
     - `epure-release-immutability` (`refs/heads/main`, `refs/tags/v*`): `Release App` as sole Bypass Actor.

---
## [EN] Basic Usage (Case Study: craft-calculator)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/basic-usage

# Basic Usage (Real-World Case Study: `craft-calculator`)

To understand how EPURE works in practice, this guide walks through a complete, anonymized real-world feature lifecycle on a TypeScript/React web application called **`my-org/craft-calculator`** (a probability and cost optimizer for an incremental crafting system).

We will follow **Issue #16** from its initial 3-line description all the way to the **`v1.0.0`** production release on `main`.

---

## Your End-to-End User Journey at a Glance

At every step of driving an issue, EPURE separates **what you do**, **what runs automatically behind the scenes**, **when EPURE pauses for your next action**, and **how autofix loops, Git conflicts, and recovery work**:

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-user-journey"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE User Journey: What I Do, Behind the Scenes, When to Act & Autofix Loops"
  caption="Interactive user-centric view of the 4 questions at every stage: your commands, automated execution, wait states, and recovery controls."
/>

| Stage | 1. What Do I Do? | 2. What Happens Behind the Scenes? | 3. When Do I Act Again & 4. How Do I Steer? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Grill & Framing** | Open the GitHub Issue, post `/epure plan`, and reply to Grill questions in plain text. | Inspects the codebase, initializes `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, and posts targeted Grill rounds until the design frontier is settled. | **Act again** after each Grill round (reply in plain text without slash commands), or run `/epure to-spec` when settled. |
| **2. Blueprint & Spec** | Comment `/epure to-spec` (and optionally post plain-text adjustments). | Creates `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, runs the zero-context **Goldfish Specification Audit**, and commits `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md` (if UI), and `docs/specs/<slug>.md`. | **Act again** once the spec draft is committed: reply in plain text to revise the spec, or comment `/epure to-tickets` when satisfied. |
| **3. Ticket DAG & Mandate** | Comment `/epure to-tickets`, review the sub-issues, then comment `/epure approve`. | Wires native GitHub `sub_issues` and `blocked_by` links, merges `plan/* -> feature/*` directly, and locks `spec_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`. | **No action required** once `/epure approve` is posted—EPURE immediately starts executing the ticket DAG. |
| **4. Autonomous Ticket Loop** | Nothing during normal execution (optional `/epure status` or `/epure sync`). | For each ticket (`task/* -> feature/*`): **Stage 1** 2-phase kernel sandbox TDD (`bwrap`/`landrun` + `rtk`) -> **Stage 2** zero-cost async CI wait (`waiting_ticket_ci`) -> **Stage 3** trusted `dev` multi-agent review + AI Semantic Squash. | **Autofix 1..3** automatically fixes Stage 1, CI, or review failures. Comment `/epure sync` for 3-way Git conflicts, or `/epure continue` if paused in `needs-human`. |
| **5. Convergence & Final Merge** | Review the final `feature/* -> dev` PR and click **Squash and merge** (plus optional `release-promote.yml` for `dev -> main`). | Runs zero-context **`EpicConvergenceAudit`** (spawning Phase 2 tickets automatically if incomplete), opens `feature/* -> dev`, and runs final synthesis CI & review. | **Act again** when the synthesis PR `feature/* -> dev` is green to perform the human Squash & Merge into `dev`. |

---

## Visual State Machine of the Issue

Throughout this walkthrough, EPURE persists the orchestration state outside standard branches inside the atomic Git reference `refs/epure/state/16`:

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-state-machine"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Issue State Machine (CAS Git Ref: refs/epure/state/<issue>)"
  caption="Atomic Compare-And-Swap transitions in refs/epure/state/16 from Grilling to Completed."
/>

---

## Step 1: Open the Issue & Start the Grill

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 1</span>

A maintainer opens **Issue #16** (*"Add exact Markov-chain crafting simulator and responsive web dashboard"*) and posts a comment:

```text
/epure plan
```

### What EPURE Does Automatically

1. **Permission Gate**: Verifies that the commenter has `write` or `admin` access to `my-org/craft-calculator`.
2. **State Initialization**: Creates `refs/epure/state/16` in phase `grilling` and adds the `EPURE Status Dashboard` at the top of Issue #16.
3. **Structured Grill Round 1**: Inspects the repository and posts 4 targeted architectural questions on Issue #16:
   - *Q1: Should expected cost be computed via Monte Carlo simulation or exact absorbing Markov chains (`45 x 45` transition matrix)?*
   - *Q2: How should irreversible corruption states be modeled in the state space?*
   - *Q3: What is the persistence model for user price presets (backend DB vs. versioned `localStorage`)?*
   - *Q4: Does the web calculator require WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and mobile responsive layout (`320px`–`1440px`)?*

### Replying to the Grill (Implicit Continuity — Q84)

Because Issue #16 is in the `grilling` phase, **you do not need to type another slash command**. Simply reply in a normal GitHub comment:

```text
1. Exact absorbing Markov chain solver (Gaussian elimination, zero Monte Carlo variance).
2. Model corruption as an absorbing failure state that triggers item replacement cost.
3. Pure client-side SPA deployed on GitHub Pages with versioned localStorage.
4. Yes, enforce WCAG 2.1 AA and mobile-first responsive layout via Impeccable.
```

> **Batch Comment Cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`, Q75)**: If you post two or three follow-up comments in a row while the runner is queued, EPURE reads all unprocessed comments in strict chronological order on startup—no comment is ever lost.

---

## Step 2: Blueprint, Goldfish Spec Audit & Native Ticket Graph (`/epure to-spec` & `/epure to-tickets`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Step</span> + <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Conditional UI Gate</span>

Once your reply settles all open questions on the design frontier, EPURE posts a **Settled Decisions Summary** and pauses in `grilling` (`awaiting_human_approval`).

1. **Generate & Audit the Specification (`/epure to-spec`)**:
   - Creates branch **`plan/16-markov-craft-calculator`** from `dev`.
   - Runs a zero-context **Goldfish Specification Audit** (`runGoldfishSpecAudit`) to verify self-containment, YAGNI discipline, and implementation readiness without Grill conversation bias, automatically amending any gaps.
   - Commits the domain and specification artifacts onto `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator`:
     - `GLOSSARY.md` (defining *Transition Matrix*, *Absorbing State*, *Expected Craft Cost*).
     - `docs/adr/0001-exact-markov-solver-and-spa.md`.
     - `DESIGN.md` (automatically generated because Issue #16 includes a UI surface, defining dark/light tokens, WCAG AA contrast, and responsive breakpoints).
     - `docs/specs/16-markov-craft-calculator.md` (complete specification including the `EpicGoalContract` entrypoints and `user-advocate` **`design-gate`** persona UX acceptance criteria).
   - Pauses in phase `spec` (`awaiting_human_approval`) so you can review or revise the spec via plain-text comments on `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator` (no intermediate `plan/* -> dev` PR is opened).
2. **Generate the Native GitHub Ticket DAG (`/epure to-tickets`)**:
   - Decomposes the validated specification into an acyclic dependency-ordered Ticket DAG on GitHub and wires native GitHub **`sub_issues`** and **`dependencies/blocked_by`** links:
     - **Issue #25**: *Core absorbing Markov solver & unit tests* (`ready-for-agent`, `blocked_by: []`)
     - **Issue #26**: *Preset price editor & versioned localStorage hook* (`ready-for-agent`, `blocked_by: [#25]`)
     - **Issue #27**: *Responsive simulator UI & Impeccable accessibility verification* (`ready-for-agent`, `blocked_by: [#25, #26]`)
   - Pauses in phase `tickets` (`awaiting_human_approval`) awaiting `/epure approve`.

---

## Step 3: Sign the Mandate (`/epure approve`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 2</span>

After reviewing the specification on `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator` and the ticket breakdown, the maintainer comments on Issue #16:

```text
/epure approve
```

### What `/epure approve` Locks In (ADR-0031, ADR-0032)

- Creates the integration branch **`feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`** from `dev` and **directly integrates the `plan/16-markov-craft-calculator` artifacts** into `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator` (with additive `GLOSSARY.md` merging and monotonic ADR renumbering if `dev` advanced, without opening a `plan/* -> dev` PR).
- Records the signed mandate in `refs/epure/state/16` (`spec_sha`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `status: "active"`).

---

## Step 4: Incremental Tools, 3-Stage Verification & Event-Driven CI (`task/* -> feature/*`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Step</span> + <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Conditional UI Gate</span>

EPURE now executes the ticket DAG in topological order (`#25`, then `#26`, then `#27`):

1. **Incremental File Mutation & Stage 1 Kernel Sandbox**:
   - Creates `task/25-markov-solver` from `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`.
   - Applies code and test changes via incremental workspace tools (`write_repo_file`, `patch_repo_file`, `delete_repo_file`) staged inside `StagedTicketImplementationBuffer` and verified by `validateTicketIntegrityGuard`.
   - Runs **Stage 1 Verification** inside the 2-phase Ubuntu 26.04 Linux kernel sandbox (`landrun` `https_only` install, offline `bwrap --unshare-net` typecheck/lint/test/build with stateless `rtk` output condensation, completely stripped of `LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys).
   - Opens **PR #28** (`task/25-markov-solver -> feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`).
2. **Stage 2 Event-Driven External CI (`waiting_ticket_ci`)**:
   - Persists `subphase: "waiting_ticket_ci"` in `refs/epure/state/16` and exits `0` immediately so no runner sits idle while GitHub Actions runs external CI on PR #28.
   - Automatically wakes up when `check_suite.completed` / `workflow_run.completed` fires on `task/25-markov-solver`.
3. **Stage 3 Multi-Agent Review (from trusted `dev`) & AI Semantic Squash**:
   - Loads the reviewer prompts (`<reviewers_dir>/*.md`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`) strictly from `dev` (never from `task/25-*`).
   - Selects up to 4 relevant reviewers (e.g., `domain-backend-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`) plus `spec-parity-reviewer`.
   - For **Ticket #27** (which touches `.tsx` and `.css` files), automatically includes `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`, `user-advocate` (`implementation-review`), and the **`impeccable-gate`** check.
   - If external CI or a reviewer emits a `must_fix`, EPURE runs a targeted remediation round (up to `max_code_fix_attempts = 3`).
   - Once green, EPURE synthesizes a Conventional Commit title and body (`feat(solver): implement exact absorbing Markov chain solver (#28)` with `Refs #25`) and performs an autonomous squash-merge via the `epure-feature-governance` ruleset.

---

## Step 5: Zero-Context `EpicConvergenceAudit`, Final Synthesis PR & Human Merge into `dev`

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Mandatory Automated Step</span> -> <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 3</span>

Once tickets `#25`, `#26`, and `#27` are merged into `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator`:

1. **Zero-Context `EpicConvergenceAudit` (`runEpicConvergenceAudit`)**: Before opening the final PR, an isolated Goldfish session audits `feature/16-markov-craft-calculator` against the specification's `EpicGoalContract` to verify that all `required_entrypoints` are wired end-to-end and no `forbidden_stubs` remain (automatically spawning Phase 2 convergence tickets if any entrypoint was left unwired).
2. EPURE opens the final synthesis **PR #47** (`feature/16-markov-craft-calculator -> dev`) with `Closes #16`, `Closes #25`, `Closes #26`, `Closes #27`.
3. Runs the full synthesis multi-agent review, `impeccable-gate`, and event-driven external CI (`waiting_feature_ci`) on the consolidated diff, updating the PR title and body with a synthesized Conventional Commit summary.
4. **Human Gate 3**: Because `epure-dev-governance` forbids the Agent App from merging code into `dev`, the human maintainer reviews PR #47 and clicks **Squash and merge**. GitHub automatically closes Issues `#16`, `#25`, `#26`, and `#27`.

---

## Step 6: Promote Release `dev -> main` (`v1.0.0`)

<span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 4</span>

When ready to cut a production release, the maintainer triggers the **`Release Promote (dev -> main)`** workflow (`workflow_dispatch` with `version: v1.0.0`), or runs via `gh`:

```bash
gh workflow run release-promote.yml -R my-org/craft-calculator -f version=v1.0.0
```

Using the isolated **Release App** (`<owner>-epure-release`), the workflow verifies that `main` is an ancestor of `dev`, performs an atomic fast-forward of `main` to `dev`, and pushes the immutable tag `v1.0.0`.

---
## [EN] Commands Reference (/epure & /setup-repo)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/commands

# Commands Reference (`/epure`, `/setup-repo` Skill & CLI)

EPURE is operated through two complementary surfaces:
1. **The local `/setup-repo` agent skill** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md` — the **preferred way** to bootstrap or reconfigure a repository, its Rulesets, and its dynamic reviewer roster in `reviewers_dir`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`).
2. **GitHub Issue slash commands (`/epure ...`)** to drive the feature lifecycle day-to-day directly from GitHub Issues.

---

## 1. GitHub Issue Slash Commands (`/epure`)

All `/epure` commands are posted as comments on a GitHub Issue. Every command is guarded by a **Fail-Closed Permission Gate**: the commenter must hold `write` or `admin` repository permissions.

| Command | Category (Q101) | Target Phase | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/epure plan` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 1</span> | `grilling` | Initializes `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, inspects the repository via read-only exploration tools (`list_repo_files`, `read_repo_file`, `search_in_repo_file`), and starts the structured architectural Grill interview. |
| *(Any human comment during Grill)* | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 1</span> | `grilling` | Implicit Grill continuity (Q84): processes human answers via the batch cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`). If follow-up questions remain (`frontier_resolved: false`), posts the next Grill round. Once all ambiguities are settled (`frontier_resolved: true`), posts a **Settled Decisions Summary** and pauses in `grilling` (`awaiting_human_approval`) so the human validates the decision frontier before `/epure to-spec`. |
| `/epure to-spec` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Human Frontier Validation</span> | `spec` | Validates the Grill decision frontier (or forces an early transition), runs the zero-context **Goldfish Specification Audit** (`runGoldfishSpecAudit`), and generates `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` (including `EpicGoalContract`) on `plan/*`, then pauses in `spec` (`awaiting_human_approval`) for human review. Free-form comments during `spec` revise the specification on `plan/*`. |
| `/epure to-tickets` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Human Spec Validation</span> | `tickets` | Validates the specification on `plan/*` and decomposes it into an acyclic dependency-ordered GitHub Issue DAG (`blocked_by`, `ready-for-agent`), wiring native GitHub relational graph links (`sub_issues` + `dependencies/blocked_by`) and pausing in `tickets` (`awaiting_human_approval`) before `/epure approve`. |
| `/epure approve` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Mandatory Human Gate 2</span> | `implementation` | Integrates the approved `plan/*` artifacts (`GLOSSARY.md` additive merge, monotonic & semantic ADR collision reconciliation, `docs/specs/<slug>.md`, `DESIGN.md`) directly into `feature/<issue>-<slug>` without an intermediate `plan/* -> dev` PR (ADR-0031, ADR-0032), locks the signed `spec_sha` mandate in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, and executes the ticket DAG (`task/* -> feature/*`). |
| `/epure continue` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Lifecycle Continuation</span> | `implementation` | Resumes orchestration after a `needs-human` suspension, after resolving a 3-way conflict, or after external CI (`waiting_ticket_ci` / `waiting_feature_ci`) completes (ADR-0031). |
| `/epure sync` (alias `/epure rebase`) | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Git Branch Sync</span> | `implementation` | Synchronizes `dev -> feature/<issue>-<slug>` (and cascades `feature/* -> active_task_branch`) with additive `GLOSSARY.md` merging, monotonic ADR reconciliation, 3-way LLM conflict resolution, and **Stage 1 Sandbox** verification before committing (ADR-0031, ADR-0032). |
| `/epure status` | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional Override</span> | *(Read-only)* | Reads `refs/epure/state/<issue>` and posts a fresh summary of the current phase, locked `spec_sha`, and per-ticket progress without mutating code. |
| `/epure cancel` (alias `/epure stop`) | <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Optional Override</span> | `cancelled` | Marks the mandate as `cancelled` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>`, stops any new ticket execution, and preserves existing branches and audit logs. |

> **Contextual `/epure` Command Cheat-Sheet Spoiler (`<details>`)**: Every issue comment, sub-issue body, and pull request description posted by EPURE automatically includes a collapsible `<details>` block at the bottom (`⌨️ Commandes /epure disponibles`) summarizing the available slash commands and highlighting the recommended next action for the current lifecycle phase (`grilling`, `spec`, `tickets`, `implementation`, `suspended`, `cancelled`, or `completed`).

---

## 2. End-to-End GitHub Actions & Custom Actions Pipeline (`epure-ci-actions-flow`)

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-ci-actions-flow"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE GitHub Actions, Custom Actions & Event-Driven CI Pipeline"
  caption="End-to-end event pipeline connecting issue_comment, check_suite/workflow_run continuation, pull_request gates, and release workflow_dispatch across secretless and environment-scoped jobs."
/>

### How Commands & CI Events Flow Through `epure-issue-command.yml`

1. **Job 1 — Secretless Authorization Gate (`authorize-command` using `actions/authorize-command`)**:
   - Triggered on `issue_comment.created` using only `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`contents: read`, `issues: write`) and **zero agent or LLM secrets**.
   - Verifies that the commenter is a human with effective `write` or `admin` permission via `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission`.
   - With `allow_implicit_planning_reply: "true"`, free-text human comments without a slash prefix are automatically routed as `reply` commands whenever the issue is in the `grilling` or `spec` phase.
2. **Job 2 — Isolated Agent Orchestration (`orchestrate-command` using `actions/orchestrate-issue`)**:
   - Runs on `ubuntu-26.04` inside the dedicated GitHub Environment (`environment: <llm-env>`, default `epure-agent`; other examples: `llm`, `openai`, `anthropic`, or `gemini`) **only after** `authorize-command` succeeds (or upon an authorized CI continuation event).
   - Receives the environment-scoped secrets (`EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, and `LLM_API_KEY` or provider key) and provisions the kernel sandbox tools (`bubblewrap`, `landrun`, `rtk`).
   - On `/epure to-tickets`, creates the child GitHub Issues and wires native GitHub relational graph links (`sub_issues` parent-child hierarchy + `dependencies/blocked_by` task edges).
3. **Automatic Event-Driven CI Continuation (`check_suite.completed` / `workflow_run.completed`)**:
   - When `async_ci_continuation: "true"` is enabled, opening a `task/* -> feature/*` PR (`waiting_ticket_ci`) or `feature/* -> dev` PR (`waiting_feature_ci`) records the active PR/SHA in `refs/epure/state/<issue>` and immediately exits `0` to free the GitHub Actions runner.
   - When external CI finishes on `task/*` or `feature/*`, the `check_suite.completed` or `workflow_run.completed` event wakes `orchestrate-command` with `command: "continue"`, `trigger_head_sha`, and `trigger_branch` to run Stage 3 multi-agent review, AI semantic squash, or unified auto-remediation.
4. **Pull Request Gates & Controlled Release Promotion**:
   - On `pull_request` events (`dev`, `main`, `feature/**`), `epure-check.yml` (`actions/epure-contract`), `pr-title.yml`, and `ci.yml` execute with `contents: read` and zero privileged secrets.
   - On human `workflow_dispatch`, `release.yml` runs inside the protected `environment: release` (`EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID`, `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) via `actions/verify-app-role` to fast-forward `dev -> main`.

---

## 3. Repository Bootstrap Agent Skill (`/setup-repo` — Recommended)

The **`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`** skill is the **preferred way** to onboard or reconfigure an EPURE consumer repository from any Skills-compatible coding agent:

```text
/setup-repo <owner>/<repo>
```

### What the `/setup-repo` Skill Does

1. **Project Discovery**: Inspects the repository stack (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`), `src/` module layout, and whether a user interface is present.
2. **Dry-Run Simulation (`--dry-run`)**: Runs `dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs --dry-run` and presents the full plan to the human maintainer before writing anything.
3. **Dynamic Reviewer Roster Design (`reviewers_dir`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`)**: Creates, designs, and tailors specialist reviewers according to the project's actual elements (always-on core `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `user-advocate` + tailored domain/UI specialists with `paths:` routing).
4. **Idempotent Application (`--apply --apply-github-settings`)**: Writes `.github/agents.yml`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `renovate.json`, SHA-pinned caller workflows, configures squash-only merges, and provisions the 3 Repository Rulesets.

---

## 4. Underlying Bootstrap CLI (`dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs`)

Invoked automatically by the `/setup-repo` skill (or runnable directly from a terminal):

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo <owner>/<name> \
  --target-dir <path> \
  [--pinned-sha <40-char-sha>] \
  [--dry-run | --apply] \
  [--apply-github-settings] \
  [--no-frontend-reviewers] \
  [--domain-reviewers <slug1,slug2>] \
  [--reviewers-dir <path>] \
  [--llm-env <env-name>] \
  [--model <provider/model>] \
  [--planning-model <provider/model>] \
  [--implementation-model <provider/model>] \
  [--review-model <provider/model>] \
  [--agent-app-id <id>] \
  [--release-app-id <id>] \
  [--require-pr-approvals <N>] \
  [--json]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--repo <owner/name>` | *(Required)* | Target GitHub repository slug (e.g., `my-org/craft-calculator`). |
| `--target-dir <path>` (aliases `--dir`, `--repo-root`) | Current directory | Local checkout path where `.github/agents.yml`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `renovate.json`, workflows, and the reviewer prompts (`<reviewers_dir>/*.md`) are written. |
| `--pinned-sha <sha>` | Latest EPURE SHA | Immutable 40-character Git commit SHA of `Giskard-AI/epure` used to pin generated caller workflows. |
| `--dry-run` | `true` (if `--apply` omitted) | Prints the complete bootstrap plan without modifying local files or calling write APIs. |
| `--apply` | `false` | Writes configuration files (`.github/agents.yml`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `renovate.json`), caller workflows, and base reviewer prompts (`<reviewers_dir>/*.md`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`). |
| `--apply-github-settings` | `false` | Applies squash-only repository settings and the 3 Repository Rulesets via the GitHub REST API. |
| `--no-frontend-reviewers` | `false` | Omits `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, and `design-reviewer` for headless repositories. |
| `--domain-reviewers <csv>` | None | Scaffolds additional `<reviewers_dir>/<slug>-reviewer.md` specialist files for domain subsystems. |
| `--reviewers-dir <path>` | `.agents/reviewers` | Reviewer roster directory written to `.github/agents.yml` (`reviewers_dir`) and read by the orchestrator from `dev` (e.g. `--reviewers-dir .cursor/agents` for a team that wants Cursor to load the reviewers as subagents). Absolute paths, `.`/`..` segments, and paths under `src/` fail closed with `SECURITY_INVARIANT_VIOLATION`. |
| `--llm-env <env-name>` | `epure-agent` | GitHub Environment name (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`) written to `.github/agents.yml` (`llm_environment`) and used by the `orchestrate-command` job of `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`. Must match the wizard's `--llm-env`. |
| `--model <provider/model>` | — | Sets `models.planning`, `models.implementation`, and `models.review` at once. |
| `--planning-model <provider/model>` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514` | Sets `models.planning`. |
| `--implementation-model <provider/model>` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514` | Sets `models.implementation`. |
| `--review-model <provider/model>` | `openai/gpt-4.1` | Sets `models.review`. |
| `--agent-app-id <id>` | Optional | Numeric GitHub App ID of `<owner>-epure-agent` added as PR Bypass Actor on `epure-feature-governance` (`feature/*`). |
| `--release-app-id <id>` | Optional | Numeric GitHub App ID of `<owner>-epure-release` added as sole Bypass Actor on `epure-release-immutability` (`main` and `v*`). |
| `--require-pr-approvals <N>` | `0` | Number of human PR review approvals required on `dev` (`0` for solo-maintainer compatibility; `>=1` for teams). |
| `--json` | `false` | Emits the full structured `SetupRepoResult` JSON payload to stdout instead of the Markdown summary. |

---

## 5. Interactive GitHub Apps Wizard (`setup-github-apps-wizard.sh`)

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh \
  --repo <owner>/<name> \
  --llm-env <env-name>
```

Guides a human maintainer through registering the two GitHub Apps (`<owner>-epure-agent` and `<owner>-epure-release`) via **Approach 2** (1-click local GitHub App Manifest flow) or **Fallback Approach 1** (manual step-by-step guided registration), creates the isolated GitHub Environments (`<llm-env>` — configurable and LLM-agnostic, default `epure-agent`; other examples: `llm`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini` — and `release`), and uploads the 5 secrets to their respective environments (`EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, and `LLM_API_KEY` in `--env <llm-env>`; `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in `--env release`).
