## [EN] Configuration (.github/agents.yml & renovate.json)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/configuration

# Configuration Reference (`.github/agents.yml`)

EPURE centralizes all orchestration, LLM routing, polyglot verification, web exploration, and non-weakenable security invariants in a single versioned declarative file: **`.github/agents.yml`**.

---

## Complete Canonical Flat Schema (`serializeAgentsConfigYaml` / `parseAgentsYaml`)

Below is the canonical flat `.github/agents.yml` file generated by `setup-repo` (`src/bootstrap/setup-repo.ts`) with all supported keys and their defaults (Q78, Q91–Q96, ADR-0028–ADR-0033):

```yaml
# EPURE Consumer Repository Configuration (.github/agents.yml)
# Generated by setup-repo — security boundaries are enforced by shared workflows (ADR-0010, ADR-0023).
harness: pi
models:
  planning: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514
  implementation: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514
  review: openai/gpt-4.1
providers:
  azure-prod:
    provider: azure
    api_key: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
    base_url: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT
    api_version: 2024-10-21
  foundry-deepseek:
    provider: azure_ai
    api_key: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_KEY
    base_url: https://my-foundry.services.ai.azure.com
merge_policy: strict
task_auto_merge_enabled: true
max_code_fix_attempts: 3
max_epic_phases: 2
max_transient_api_retries: 4
transient_retry_backoff_seconds: [5, 15, 45, 120]
llm_request_timeout_seconds: 900
job_timeout_minutes: 60
review_timeout_minutes: 30
max_concurrent_tasks_per_feature: 3
trace_retention_days: 30
preview_retention_days: 14
github_pages_previews: false
reviewers_dir: .agents/reviewers
llm_environment: epure-agent
verification:
  wait_for_external_ci: true
  external_ci_timeout_minutes: 15
  grace_window_seconds: 45
  targets:
    - name: root
      working_directory: .
      kind: node
      path_patterns: ["**"]
      install_command: "npm ci --ignore-scripts"
      typecheck_command: "npm run typecheck"
      lint_command: "npm run lint"
      test_command: "npm test"
      build_command: "npm run build"
web_tools:
  enabled: true
  phases: ["plan", "spec", "implementation"]
  max_requests_per_turn: 4
  max_requests_per_run: 12
  max_bytes_per_response: 16384
  max_fetch_bytes: 16384
  timeout_ms: 10000
security_invariants:
  require_write_permission: true
  sandbox_isolation: true
  allow_agent_release: false
  auto_merge_dev: false
  auto_merge_main: false
```

---

## Configurable & LLM-Agnostic GitHub Environment (`<llm-env>`)

In `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`, the `orchestrate-command` job runs inside a dedicated GitHub Environment (`environment: <llm-env>`) **only after** the secretless `authorize-command` job verifies effective `write` or `admin` permission:

- **Free & Provider-Agnostic Naming**: The `<llm-env>` environment name defaults to **`epure-agent`** (`llm_environment` in `.github/agents.yml`) and is completely configurable via `setup-repo --llm-env <env-name>` and `setup-github-apps-wizard.sh --llm-env <env-name>` (use the same value for both). It is agnostic of the underlying LLM provider (other examples: `llm`, `openai`, `anthropic`, or `gemini`) and must only contain `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`.
- **Zizmor-Compliant Secret Isolation**: `EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, and `LLM_API_KEY` (or custom provider secret referenced via `os.environ/VAR_NAME`) are scoped strictly to `--env <llm-env>`, while `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are scoped to the human-approved `--env release` environment. Public pull request workflows and `authorize-command` never have access to any secret.

---

## Section-by-Section Reference

### Root Execution, Retry & Governance Keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `harness` | `"pi" \| "codex"` | `"pi"` | Agent execution adapter harness used for sandboxed runs. |
| `merge_policy` | `"strict" \| "relaxed"` | `"strict"` | Stale-base policy for `task/* -> feature/*` integration (`strict` requires up-to-date base; `relaxed` allows clean 3-way merge when approved diff is unchanged). |
| `task_auto_merge_enabled` | `boolean` | `false` (`true` when CI & branch protections exist) | Enables autonomous squash-merge of validated `task/* -> feature/*` PRs; forced to `false` (`AUTO_MERGE_DISABLED_MISSING_PROTECTIONS`) if required CI or branch protections are missing. |
| `max_code_fix_attempts` | `integer` | `3` | Maximum number of automated remediation rounds (Stage 1 sandbox, external CI, or multi-agent review) per ticket before escalating to `needs-human` (Q78). |
| `max_epic_phases` | `integer` (`1..3`) | `2` | Maximum number of epic execution phases when `runEpicConvergenceAudit` detects unwired entrypoints (`[Phase 2 - Ticket N]`, ADR-0032). |
| `max_transient_api_retries` | `integer` | `4` | Per-HTTP-request retry ceiling for transient LLM errors (`5xx`, `408`, network timeout). `HTTP 429` rate limits honor `Retry-After` (up to 10 waits) without consuming this quota. |
| `transient_retry_backoff_seconds` | `[int, int, int, int]` | `[5, 15, 45, 120]` | Exponential backoff schedule in seconds between transient HTTP retries. |
| `llm_request_timeout_seconds` | `integer` | `900` | Unitary HTTP request timeout in seconds (`15 minutes`) for each LLM API call. |
| `job_timeout_minutes` | `integer` | `60` | Wall-clock timeout in minutes for `orchestrate-command` in `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml` (Q78). |
| `review_timeout_minutes` | `integer` | `30` | Timeout in minutes for multi-agent PR review jobs (with up to `max_parallel_reviewers = 4` specialist/transverse reviewers selected per PR diff alongside `spec-parity-reviewer`). |
| `max_concurrent_tasks_per_feature` | `integer` | `3` | Maximum number of unblocked `task/*` tickets executed concurrently per `feature/*` branch. |
| `trace_retention_days` | `integer` | `30` | Retention period in days for minimized audit trajectories (`iFixAi`). |
| `preview_retention_days` | `integer` | `14` | Number of days before hosted `/prototype` previews are automatically purged (Q71). |
| `github_pages_previews` | `boolean` | `false` | Opt-in flag (legacy alias `enable_pages_preview: false`) to publish static `/prototype` previews to an isolated GitHub Pages origin; requires `github_pages_human_consent: true` and `preview_separate_origin: true` (Q70, Q73). |
| `reviewers_dir` | `string` (relative path) | `".agents/reviewers"` | Reviewer roster directory where `setup-repo` writes and the orchestrator reads reviewer prompt files `<name>.md` (always from the trusted `dev` branch, falling back to EPURE's embedded templates). Configurable via `setup-repo --reviewers-dir <path>` (for example `.cursor/agents` for a team that wants Cursor to load the reviewers as subagents). Absolute paths, paths with `.` or `..` segments, and paths under `src/` are rejected fail-closed with `SECURITY_INVARIANT_VIOLATION`. |
| `llm_environment` | `string` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`) | `"epure-agent"` | GitHub Environment name used by the `orchestrate-command` job of the generated `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml` (`environment: <llm-env>`). Configurable via `setup-repo --llm-env <name>`; must match the environment created by `setup-github-apps-wizard.sh --llm-env <name>`. |

### `models` & `providers` (Multi-Provider Routing — ADR-0029)

EPURE includes a zero-dependency multi-provider `LLMClient` supporting **Google Gemini** (`google/` or `gemini/`), **OpenAI** (`openai/`), **Azure OpenAI** (`azure/`), **Azure AI Foundry** (`azure_ai/`), and **Anthropic** (`anthropic/`).

`models.planning`, `models.implementation`, and `models.review` are **required**: EPURE has no fallback model, consistent with ADR-0012's no-automatic-fallback principle. A non-empty `model` input on the `orchestrate-issue` action overrides all three phases; otherwise each phase uses its `models.<phase>` value verbatim. When a command that calls an LLM finds a key missing, it suspends with a `needs-human` escalation (`model_config_missing`) naming the key to set, before any LLM call; commands that make no LLM call (`status`, `cancel`, replies outside grilling/spec, `continue` with nothing waiting) are unaffected. EPURE reads `.github/agents.yml` from `dev` (from `main` only when `dev` has no such file); a file that fails to parse is never ignored or replaced by the `main` copy: commands that call an LLM escalate to `needs-human` with the parser message (`Invalid .github/agents.yml on 'dev': ...`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `models.planning` | `string` | *(Required; `setup-repo` writes `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`)* | Model used for `/epure plan` Grill interviews, `/epure to-spec` / `/epure to-tickets`, and plan-to-feature ADR reconciliation (`<provider>/<model>` or bare model). Override with `setup-repo --planning-model` (or `--model` for all phases). |
| `models.implementation` | `string` | *(Required; `setup-repo` writes `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`)* | Model used for incremental workspace tool loops (`write_repo_file`, `patch_repo_file`), 3-way conflict resolution, `/epure sync` ADR reconciliation, and Stage 1/2/3 auto-remediation. Override with `setup-repo --implementation-model` (or `--model`). |
| `models.review` | `string` | *(Required; `setup-repo` writes `"openai/gpt-4.1"`)* | Model used for the multi-agent PR review roster, `runGoldfishSpecAudit`, `runEpicConvergenceAudit`, `user-advocate`, and squash commit synthesis (requested at temperature `0.0`; no temperature is sent to Claude Opus 4.7+ / Claude 5.x+). Override with `setup-repo --review-model` (or `--model`). |
| `providers.<alias>.provider` | `"google" \| "openai" \| "azure" \| "azure_ai" \| "anthropic"` | *(Optional)* | Underlying protocol family for a custom provider alias referenced in `models.*` (`<alias>/<model>`). |
| `providers.<alias>.api_key` | `string` | `os.environ/<VAR>` | Secret-free environment variable reference (`os.environ/VAR_NAME`) resolved at runtime from `process.env`. Never commit literal API keys in `.github/agents.yml`. |
| `providers.<alias>.base_url` | `string` | Provider default | Custom base URL or `os.environ/VAR_NAME`. |
| `providers.<alias>.api_version` | `string` | `"2024-10-21"` | Azure OpenAI deployment API version (`?api-version=...`). |
| `providers.<alias>.default_headers` | `Record<string, string>` | `{}` | Optional custom HTTP headers attached to every request for this provider alias. |
| `providers.<alias>.effort` | `"low" \| "medium" \| "high" \| "xhigh" \| "max"` | *(Optional, model default)* | Anthropic only: sent as `output_config.effort` on every request for every model routed through this alias (e.g. `effort: high` for `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). Omitted when unset. Any other value makes `.github/agents.yml` invalid: commands that call an LLM escalate to `needs-human` with the parse error. `temperature` is automatically omitted for Claude Opus 4.7+ and Claude 5.x+ models, which reject sampling parameters. |

An Anthropic response with `stop_reason: refusal` raises an `LLMError` with `reasonCode: "REFUSAL"`. It is not retried: the orchestrator suspends with a `needs-human` escalation (`llm_refusal`) without consuming the ticket's `max_code_fix_attempts` budget.

### `verification` & `verification.targets` (Polyglot Stage 1 & Stage 2 CI — ADR-0028, ADR-0030)

Always loaded at runtime from the trusted `dev` branch so an untrusted `task/*` branch can never weaken its own test commands:

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `verification.wait_for_external_ci` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables Stage 2 external CI waiting (`waiting_ticket_ci` / `waiting_feature_ci`) on `task/*` and `feature/*` PRs. |
| `verification.external_ci_timeout_minutes` | `integer` | `15` | Maximum external CI wait ceiling in minutes before timeout classification. |
| `verification.grace_window_seconds` | `integer` | `45` | Grace window in seconds after PR push to allow GitHub Actions check runs to register before evaluating completion. |
| `verification.deferred_external_workflows` | `string[]` | `[]` | Optional workflow names deferred from per-ticket `task/*` blocking and enforced only on `feature/* -> dev`. |
| `verification.targets` | `VerificationTargetSpec[]` | Auto-discovered by `setup-repo` | Per-subproject Stage 1 verification targets (`name`, `working_directory`, `kind`: `node \| python \| rust \| go \| make \| custom`, `path_patterns`, `install_command`, `codegen_command`, `typecheck_command`, `lint_command`, `test_command`, `build_command`) executed inside the 2-phase Ubuntu 26.04 kernel sandbox (`landrun` + `bubblewrap`). |

### `web_tools` (Confined Public Web Exploration — ADR-0031)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web_tools.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Enables zero-API-key read-only public Web exploration tools (`web_search`, `web_fetch`) constrained to `https://` port `443` with strict Anti-SSRF filtering and `<untrusted_web_content>` wrapping. |
| `web_tools.phases` | `string[]` | `["plan", "spec", "implementation"]` | Lifecycle phases allowed to invoke `web_search` and `web_fetch` (excluded from `review` by default). |
| `web_tools.max_requests_per_turn` | `integer` | `4` | Maximum Web tool requests permitted within a single LLM turn. |
| `web_tools.max_requests_per_run` | `integer` | `12` | Maximum Web tool requests permitted across an entire orchestrator run. |
| `web_tools.max_bytes_per_response` | `integer` | `16384` | Maximum UTF-8 byte budget returned per tool response. |
| `web_tools.max_fetch_bytes` | `integer` | `16384` | Maximum UTF-8 byte budget returned per `web_fetch` call after HTML stripping. |
| `web_tools.timeout_ms` | `integer` | `10000` | Per-request HTTP timeout in milliseconds for Web exploration calls. |

### `security_invariants` & Sensitive Paths

Any attempt in `.github/agents.yml` to weaken `security_invariants` (`require_write_permission: false`, `sandbox_isolation: false`, `allow_agent_release: true`, `auto_merge_dev: true`, `auto_merge_main: true`) is rejected fail-closed with `SECURITY_INVARIANT_VIOLATION`. Furthermore, any modification to `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/agents.yml`, the reviewer roster directory (the configured `reviewers_dir/**` and the default `.agents/reviewers/**`), or `CODEOWNERS` on a `task/*` branch triggers a **Sensitive Path Escalation** (`needs-human`) unless a maintainer explicitly adds the `approved-sensitive-change` label (Q81, Q93).

---

## Supply-Chain & Renovate Security Policy (`renovate.json` & `.github/zizmor.yml`)

Every EPURE repository ships a hardened **`renovate.json`** and **`.github/zizmor.yml`** generated by `/setup-repo` (Q46–Q48):

- **Quarantine Cooldown (No Day-1 Merges)**: Enforces `minimumReleaseAge: "3 days"` globally (`"7 days"` for minor updates and GitHub Actions/Docker images, `"14 days"` for major npm updates) coupled with `internalChecksFilter: "strict"` and `prCreation: "not-pending"` so newly published or compromised packages are quarantined before any PR is opened.
- **Maximum Safe Automation**: Groups minor, patch, pin, and digest updates into single weekly PRs (`npm-minor-and-patch`, `github-actions`, `docker`), pins exact versions (`rangeStrategy: "pin"`, `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`, `docker:pinDigests`), runs monthly `lockFileMaintenance`, and automatically rebases behind `dev` (`rebaseWhen: "behind-base-branch"`).
- **Post-Install Script Isolation**: Injects `npmrc: "ignore-scripts=true"` during Renovate lockfile resolution to prevent untrusted lifecycle scripts from executing.
- **No Unreviewed Auto-Merge into `dev`**: `automerge: false` and `platformAutomerge: false` are strictly enforced; Renovate PRs target `dev`, run the full CI + multi-agent review pipeline, and optionally trigger the assisted `auto_migrate` agent if a breaking change is detected on a verified Renovate App PR.

---
## [EN] Architecture, Security & Multi-Agent Review
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/architecture

# Architecture, Security & Multi-Agent Review Model

EPURE is built from the ground up around **Defense-in-Depth**, **Least Privilege**, and **Out-of-Branch Deterministic State**. Every automation boundary is enforced both by GitHub Repository Rulesets and by local runtime sandboxing.

> **Interactive Event & Custom Actions Pipeline Diagram**: See the [`epure-ci-actions-flow` diagram in Commands Reference](./commands#2-end-to-end-github-actions-custom-actions-pipeline-epure-ci-actions-flow) for the complete mapping of GitHub events (`issue_comment`, `check_suite`, `workflow_run`, `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`), secretless `authorize-command`, environment-scoped `orchestrate-command` (`environment: <llm-env>`), and `release` promotion.

---

## 1. Security & Trust Boundaries Architecture

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-security-architecture"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Security & Trust Boundaries Architecture"
  caption="Interactive architecture diagram showing the Trusted Control Plane, Secretless Sandbox, Out-of-Branch CAS State, and Dual GitHub Apps."
/>

### Key Architectural Invariants

1. **Dual GitHub App Separation & Environment-Scoped Secrets (`<owner>-epure-agent` vs. `<owner>-epure-release`, Q82 & Q91)**:
   - The **Agent App** mints short-lived RS256 installation tokens scoped to day-to-day orchestration (`plan/*`, `task/*`, `feature/*`). Its credentials (`EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) and `LLM_API_KEY` are scoped to the dedicated agent GitHub Environment (`<llm-env>`) and never exposed to `authorize-command` or public PR workflows. It is a Bypass Actor **only** on `epure-feature-governance` (`refs/heads/feature/*`), allowing autonomous integration of verified atomic tasks while physically blocking it from merging application code into `dev` or pushing to `main`.
   - The **Release App** is invoked exclusively by `release-promote.yml` / `release.yml` under human `workflow_dispatch` inside the protected `release` GitHub Environment (`EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID`, `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`). It is the sole Bypass Actor on `epure-release-immutability` (`refs/heads/main` and `refs/tags/v*`).
2. **Secretless Sandbox Execution (Q74)**:
   - When EPURE runs `npm test`, `npm run build`, or `pytest` on a `task/*` branch, the child process environment is scrubbed of `LLM_API_KEY`, `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
   - A malicious or compromised test script cannot exfiltrate credentials. If sandbox isolation fails, EPURE aborts **fail-closed**.
3. **Out-of-Branch CAS State (`refs/epure/state/<issue>`, Q76)**:
   - State transitions (`last_processed_comment_id`, signed `spec_sha`, retry counters, ticket status table, and active CI continuation subphases) are stored as JSON blobs inside `refs/epure/state/<issue-number>` updated via atomic `git update-ref` Compare-And-Swap.
   - `dev` and `main` remain 100% free of machine-state commit noise.

---

## 2. Multi-Agent PR Review, Impeccable Gate & AI Squash Pipeline

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-review-pipeline"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE Multi-Agent PR Review, Impeccable Gate & Semantic Squash Pipeline"
  caption="Trusted dev roster loading, read-only code inspection tools, Impeccable UI gate, and targeted remediation loop."
/>

### How the Review Pipeline Works (Q92–Q96)

1. **Trusted `dev` Roster Loading & Prompt-Injection Defense (OWASP LLM01)**:
   - Reviewer prompts (`<reviewers_dir>/*.md`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`) are **always** loaded from the trusted `dev` branch (with fallback to EPURE's embedded canonical templates), never from the untrusted `task/*` branch under review.
   - All PR diffs, commit messages, and issue comments are wrapped inside `<untrusted_pr_diff>` XML delimiters with explicit instructions to ignore any embedded prompt-override directives.
2. **Dynamic Selection (Up to 4 Specialists + `spec-parity-reviewer`)**:
   - Based on the files touched in the PR diff, EPURE selects up to 4 relevant reviewers from the roster (`domain-backend-reviewer`, `frontend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`, `user-advocate`) alongside the mandatory `spec-parity-reviewer`.
3. **Read-Only Codebase Inspection Tools**:
   - Reviewers are not restricted to a narrow unified diff: they can invoke 4 read-only tools (`list_files`, `read_file`, `read_line_range`, `search_code`) to trace callers, types, and domain invariants across the repository.
4. **Targeted Auto-Remediation (`max_code_fix_attempts = 3`)**:
   - If any reviewer emits a `must_fix` item, EPURE runs a targeted code fix in the secretless sandbox and re-runs **only** the reviewers that failed in the previous round plus `spec-parity-reviewer`.
   - On `feature/* -> dev` synthesis PRs, any remediation is routed through a `task/review-fix-*` PR so `epure-feature-governance` is respected.
5. **AI Semantic Squash Synthesis (Q94)**:
   - Immediately before merging a validated PR, a zero-temperature call synthesizes a clean Conventional Commit title (`type(scope): summary (#PR)`) and bulleted body (`Refs #<ticket>` on `feature/*`, `Closes #<issue>` / `Closes #<ticket>` on `dev`).
6. **Integrated Upstream Quality & Audit Engines**:
   - **[Matt Pocock Agent Skills (`mattpocock/skills`)](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)** — Specification-driven skills (`grill-with-docs`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `tdd`, `code-review`) pinned in `skills-lock.json`.
   - **[Impeccable (`pbakaus/impeccable`)](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** — Design system (`DESIGN.md`) and WCAG 2.1 AA frontend quality gate (`actions/impeccable`).
   - **[iFixAi (`ifixai-ai/iFixAi`)](https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi)** — Deterministic authorization trajectory auditing (`actions/ifixai`).
   - **[Archify (`tt-a1i/archify`)](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** — Showcase-validated interactive architecture diagrams (`scripts/archify/`).
   - **[zizmor (`woodruffw/zizmor`)](https://github.com/woodruffw/zizmor)** — GitHub Actions workflow static security analysis (`actions/zizmor-audit`).
   - **[Renovate (`renovatebot/renovate`)](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate)** — Automated updates of SHA-pinned workflows and dependencies (`auto_migrate`).

---

## 3. Multi-Provider `LLMClient`, Native Structured Outputs & Modular Orchestrator (ADR-0029)

1. **Multi-Provider HTTP Router (`src/llm/`)**:
   - Zero-dependency TypeScript `LLMClient` routing `<provider>/<model>` identifiers across **Google Gemini** (`google/`, `gemini/`), **OpenAI** (`openai/`), **Azure OpenAI** (`azure/`), **Azure AI Foundry** (`azure_ai/`), and **Anthropic** (`anthropic/`), with `os.environ/VAR_NAME` lazy resolution from `.github/agents.yml`.
   - Enforces ADR-0012 fail-fast resilience: HTTP `401`/`403` (`AuthenticationError`) and `402` (`QuotaExhaustedError`) immediately halt without silent fallback, while transient `408`/`429`/`5xx` errors apply bounded exponential backoff.
2. **Native Schema-Enforced Structured Outputs (`ResponseSchemaSpec<T>`) & 2-Phase Gemini Tool Loop**:
   - All structured LLM calls (`GrillRoundEvaluation`, `GeneratedPlanningBundle`, `GeneratedTicketImplementation`, multi-agent reviewer findings, `user-advocate`, and squash commit synthesis) send formal JSON Schemas (`responseSchema`, `response_format.json_schema` with recursive `additionalProperties: false`, or `output_config.format`) paired with runtime TypeScript validators in `src/orchestrator/prompts/schemas.ts`.
   - When Google Gemini calls combine repository exploration tools (`list_repo_files`, `search_in_repo_file`, `read_repo_file`) with a `ResponseSchemaSpec`, **Phase 1** executes tool rounds with `functionDeclarations` (preserving Gemini 3 `thoughtSignature` tokens), and **Phase 2** finalizes with `functionCallingConfig.mode = "NONE"` + `responseMimeType: "application/json"` + `responseSchema`.
3. **Modular `src/orchestrator/` Architecture & Wired Safety Guards**:
   - `src/orchestrator/issue-orchestrator.ts` acts as a clean coordinator delegating to `github/rest-client.ts`, `workspace/repo-tools.ts`, `prompts/schemas.ts`, `formatting/comments.ts`, and the phase modules `phases/grill-and-plan.ts`, `phases/ticket-execution.ts`, and `phases/feature-integration.ts`.
   - Enforces DAG cycle detection (`validatePlanningArtifactsAndGraph`), proven blocker resolution (`reconcileProvenTicketDependencies`, escalating to `needs-human` on `not_planned` closures), mid-run `/epure cancel` batch cursor checks (`processPendingIssueCommentsBatch`), and commit-SHA review loop guards (`evaluateReviewFeedbackTrigger`).

---

## 4. 3-Stage Verification Pipeline, Ubuntu 26.04 Kernel Sandbox & Event-Driven CI Continuation (ADR-0028, ADR-0030, ADR-0031)

1. **Stage 1 — 2-Phase Linux Kernel Sandbox, Stateless `rtk` Condensation & Per-Ticket Goldfish Isolation**:
   - Runs on `ubuntu-26.04` (Linux kernel 7.0) inside a persistent local Git clone before any commit is pushed to `task/*`:
     - **Phase A (`install`, `networkPolicy: "https_only"`)**: Executes dependency installation under `landrun` (Landlock ABI v8), restricting outbound TCP to port `443` and filesystem writes to `workDir`, `/tmp`, and package caches.
     - **Phase B (`codegen`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`, `networkPolicy: "offline"`)**: Executes completely offline under `bubblewrap` (`bwrap --unshare-net --unshare-pid --unshare-ipc --tmpfs /tmp --die-with-parent`, with automatic fallback to offline `landrun`).
   - **Stateless `rtk` Output Condensation (`formatAndCondenseStage1CommandOutput`)**: Strips ANSI sequences, progress bars, and noisy test logs in 100% stateless mode (`RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `RTK_RECALL=0`, `RTK_TEE=0`, no SQLite database) while preserving the raw 4,000-character error tail whenever `exit_code !== 0`.
   - **3-Way Git Branch Sync (`/epure sync`) & Goldfish Isolation**: Keeps `dev -> feature/* -> task/*` synchronized with 3-way LLM conflict resolution validated by Stage 1, and executes each ticket in a fresh zero-context Goldfish session (`runGoldfishSpecAudit` during `/epure to-spec`).
2. **Stage 2 — Event-Driven External CI Continuation (`waiting_ticket_ci` / `waiting_feature_ci`)**:
   - Once Stage 1 passes and the `task/* -> feature/*` or `feature/* -> dev` Pull Request is opened alongside the `ai-review` check, EPURE records `subphase: "waiting_ticket_ci"` (or `"waiting_feature_ci"`), `active_pr_number`, and `active_head_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>` and immediately exits `0` (`async_ci_continuation: true`).
   - No runner sits idle polling external workflows. When GitHub emits `check_suite.completed` or `workflow_run.completed` (or a human posts `/epure continue`), EPURE resumes from the exact persisted state.
3. **Stage 3 — Trusted `dev` Multi-Agent Review Roster & AI Semantic Squash**:
   - Correlates external CI results with the multi-agent specialist review roster loaded from `dev`. If external CI or any reviewer fails, EPURE extracts sanitized failure logs (~12 KB) and executes up to `max_code_fix_attempts = 3` unified remediation rounds before AI semantic squash-merging `task/* -> feature/*`.

---

## 5. Incremental Workspace Mutation Tools, Inter-Ticket Guard & Multi-Phase Epic Convergence (ADR-0032, ADR-0033)

1. **Transactional Incremental Workspace Mutation (`StagedTicketImplementationBuffer`)**:
   - During ticket implementation and remediation tool loops, the model mutates files incrementally via `write_repo_file`, `patch_repo_file`, and `delete_repo_file` inside an in-memory transactional buffer (`StagedTicketImplementationBuffer`), isolated from `feature/*` until `validateWorkspaceFileOperations`, `validateTicketIntegrityGuard`, and Stage 1 sandbox checks succeed.
   - **Chunked File-by-File Fallback (`ChunkedTicketImplementationFallback`)**: If a multi-file ticket hits `MAX_TOKENS` output truncation, EPURE automatically decomposes the remaining `filesToTouch` entries into file-by-file sub-calls (preserving already staged mutations in the buffer and rolling back atomically if any sub-call fails).
   - **Zero-Truncation Context Catalog (`CompactWorkspaceFilesContext`)**: Injects full, untruncated file contents only for files modified by the ticket or listed in `filesToTouch`, and exposes the rest of the repository as a compact `path (N lines)` index inspectable on demand via `read_repo_file` and `search_in_repo_file`.
2. **Native GitHub Relational Graph, Inter-Ticket Integrity Guard & Semantic ADR Reconciliation**:
   - `/epure to-tickets` wires native GitHub `sub_issues` and `dependencies/blocked_by` relationships alongside the Markdown tasklist on the tracking issue.
   - `validateTicketIntegrityGuard` blocks any ticket from deleting or emptying pre-existing test files, truncating >30% of lines/exports on out-of-scope files, or downgrading manifest `build`/`test`/`lint`/`typecheck` scripts into no-op commands.
   - `renumberCollidingAdrs` and `reconcileAdrsWithLlm` deduplicate ADR slugs across concurrent branches, renumber colliding `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` files monotonically, and align cross-references in specs and `GLOSSARY.md`.
3. **Zero-Context `EpicConvergenceAudit` & Multi-Phase Remediation (`max_epic_phases`)**:
   - Before opening the final `feature/* -> dev` PR, an isolated zero-context session (`runEpicConvergenceAudit`) verifies the feature branch against the specification's `EpicGoalContract` (`required_entrypoints`, absence of `forbidden_stubs`, and `end_to_end_verification_criteria`).
   - If unwired modules or stubs are detected (`verdict: "INCOMPLETE"`) and `epic_phase < max_epic_phases` (default `2`), EPURE automatically generates, links, and executes bounded **Phase 2 convergence tickets** (`[Phase 2 - Ticket N]`) before opening the final PR; otherwise it escalates with `epic_convergence_exhausted` (`needs-human`).

---
## [EN] How-To: Onboard a Repository
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-onboard-repo

# How-To: Onboard a Repository with the `/setup-repo` Skill

This guide shows how to take a brand-new or existing GitHub repository (such as `my-org/craft-calculator`) and onboard it by invoking **the `/setup-repo` agent skill** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`)—the preferred way to configure EPURE's 2 GitHub Apps, environment-scoped secrets (`<llm-env>` and `release`), `.github/agents.yml`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `renovate.json`, dynamic reviewer roster (`reviewers_dir`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`), and 3 Repository Rulesets.

---

## 1. Create the Two GitHub Apps & Environment-Scoped Secrets

EPURE separates day-to-day agent privileges from production release privileges using two GitHub Apps and scopes all secrets to dedicated GitHub Environments (Zizmor-compliant zero global secret exposure):

- **`<owner>-epure-agent`**: Permissions `contents: write`, `issues: write`, `pull_requests: write`, `checks: write`.
- **`<owner>-epure-release`**: Permissions `contents: write`, `metadata: read`.

Run the interactive wizard (supports **Approach 2** 1-click GitHub App Manifest Flow and **Fallback Approach 1** manual guided mode), specifying your target repository and chosen agent environment name (`--llm-env <env-name>`, default `epure-agent`; other examples: `llm`, `openai`, `anthropic`, or `gemini`):

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --llm-env <llm-env>
```

Verify that the secrets are registered in their respective GitHub Environments:

```bash
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator --env <llm-env>
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator --env release
```

Expected output for `--env <llm-env>`:

```text
EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID
EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
LLM_API_KEY
```

Expected output for `--env release`:

```text
EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID
EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
```

---

## 2. Invoke the `/setup-repo` Skill (Inspection & `--dry-run` Simulation)

Inside your Skills-compatible coding agent, invoke the **`/setup-repo`** skill on the target repository:

```text
/setup-repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

The agent inspects the repository's elements (language, build scripts, UI presence, sub-domains in `src/`) and first runs the CLI in `--dry-run` mode:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --dry-run
```

Check that the dry-run report presented by the agent lists:

- Creation of `.github/agents.yml` (flat canonical schema with auto-discovered `verification.targets`), `.github/zizmor.yml`, and `renovate.json`.
- Creation of `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`, `epure-check.yml`, `pr-title.yml`, `ci.yml`, and `release.yml` pinned to the 40-character SHA of `Giskard-AI/epure`.
- Dynamic initialization of the reviewer roster in `.agents/reviewers/*.md` (or the `--reviewers-dir` you chose) designed by the agent for your stack and sub-domains (always-on core `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer`, `user-advocate` + tailored domain/UI specialists, yielding 10 agents for the `craft-calculator` web app example).
- Creation of the 3 Repository Rulesets (`epure-feature-governance`, `epure-dev-governance`, `epure-release-immutability`).

---

## 3. Confirm Application (`--apply`) & Commit to `dev`

Once you confirm, the `/setup-repo` skill runs `--apply --apply-github-settings` and tailors the `<reviewers_dir>/<role>-reviewer.md` definitions to your domain modules:

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /path/to/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --apply \
  --apply-github-settings
```

Then commit and push the generated files (`.github/`, `.agents/reviewers/`, and `renovate.json`) to `dev`:

```bash
cd /path/to/craft-calculator
git checkout dev
git add .github/ .agents/reviewers/ renovate.json
git commit -m "chore(epure): bootstrap repository governance and workflows"
git push origin dev
```

---

## 4. Solo Maintainer vs. Team Mode (`--require-pr-approvals`)

- **Solo Maintainer (Default `--require-pr-approvals 0`)**: GitHub does not allow a user to approve their own Pull Request. Setting `required_approving_review_count: 0` on `epure-dev-governance` ensures you can click **Squash and merge** on `feature/* -> dev` PRs opened by EPURE while still blocking the `Agent App` from self-merging.
- **Multi-Maintainer Team (`--require-pr-approvals 1` or higher)**: Require at least one peer human approval in addition to green `verify-contract` and `ai-review` checks before merging into `dev`.

---
## [EN] How-To: Drive an Issue End-to-End
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-drive-an-issue

# How-To: Drive an Issue End-to-End

This guide provides a practical checklist for steering a feature or complex bugfix from an initial GitHub Issue to a ready-to-merge `feature/* -> dev` Pull Request, including optional overrides and failure recovery.

---

## 1. Launching the Plan (`/epure plan`)

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-user-journey"
  locale="en"
  title="EPURE User Journey: Driving an Issue from Idea to Merged PR"
  caption="Complete user journey across 4 lanes: 1. What I Do -> 2. What Happens Behind the Scenes -> 3. When I Act Again -> 4. Autofix Loops, Conflicts & Steering."
/>

1. Open a GitHub Issue describing the goal, user problem, or feature scope.
2. Post `/epure plan` in a comment.
3. Wait for the `epure-issue-command` workflow to post **Grill Round 1**.

### Tips for Answering the Grill

- **Reply in plain Markdown**: You do not need to prefix your answers with `/epure` while the issue is in phase `grilling`.
- **Multiple comments are safe**: Thanks to the batch cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`), if you add a second comment with an extra constraint while a run is queued, EPURE will process both comments in order.
- **Short-circuiting the Grill (Optional)**: If you feel the questions are already answered and want to jump straight to specification generation, comment `/epure to-spec`.

---

## 2. Generating & Reviewing the Specification (`/epure to-spec` & `/epure to-tickets`)

Once the Grill decision frontier is resolved (`frontier_resolved: true`), EPURE posts a **Settled Decisions Summary** and pauses in `grilling` (`awaiting_human_approval`).

1. **Generate the Specification (`/epure to-spec`)**: Comment `/epure to-spec` to run the zero-context **Goldfish Specification Audit** (`runGoldfishSpecAudit`) and commit `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md`, `DESIGN.md` (if UI is involved), and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` (including `EpicGoalContract`) onto `plan/<issue>-<slug>`. The issue transitions to `spec` (`awaiting_human_approval`).
2. **Revise or Validate the Specification**:
   - Inspect `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` on `plan/<issue>-<slug>`.
   - To request adjustments to the specification before creating tickets, **reply directly in a comment** (without a slash command).
3. **Generate the Ticket DAG (`/epure to-tickets`)**: Once the specification is approved, comment `/epure to-tickets`. EPURE decomposes the spec into an acyclic dependency-ordered GitHub Issue DAG (`blocked_by`, `ready-for-agent`), wires native GitHub `sub_issues` and `dependencies/blocked_by` graph links, and pauses in `tickets` (`awaiting_human_approval`) awaiting `/epure approve`.

---

## 3. Approving, Event-Driven CI Continuation & Branch Sync (`/epure approve`, `/epure status` & `/epure sync`)

Post `/epure approve` on the tracking issue to directly integrate the `plan/*` artifacts into `feature/<issue>-<slug>`, lock `spec_sha`, and start executing the ticket DAG.

- **Event-Driven External CI Waiting (`waiting_ticket_ci` / `waiting_feature_ci`)**:
  - Whenever EPURE opens a `task/* -> feature/*` PR (`waiting_ticket_ci`) or the final `feature/* -> dev` PR (`waiting_feature_ci`), the orchestrator records the active PR and `head_sha` in `refs/epure/state/<issue>` and immediately exits `0` to release the GitHub Actions runner (`async_ci_continuation: true`).
  - As soon as external CI workflows complete (`check_suite.completed` or `workflow_run.completed`), EPURE automatically wakes up to run Stage 3 multi-agent review, AI semantic squash, or unified auto-remediation. You can also manually nudge continuation at any time by commenting **`/epure continue`**.
- **Synchronizing with `dev` (`/epure sync` / `/epure rebase`)**:
  - If other PRs land on `dev` while your feature is in progress, comment **`/epure sync`** (or `/epure rebase`). EPURE merges `dev -> feature/<issue>-<slug>` (and cascades `feature/* -> active_task_branch`) with additive `GLOSSARY.md` merging, monotonic ADR renumbering, 3-way LLM conflict resolution, and mandatory **Stage 1 Kernel Sandbox** verification before committing.
- **Inspecting Live Progress (`/epure status`)**:
  - Comment `/epure status` or check the **EPURE Status Dashboard** pinned at the top of the issue body.
  - Inside the GitHub Actions run logs, expand the structured `::group::` sections to inspect Stage 1 kernel sandbox test/build output, read-only reviewer tool calls (`read_file`, `search_code`), and per-reviewer verdicts (`approved` vs. `changes_requested`).

---

## 4. Handling `needs-human` Escalations, `/epure continue` & Phase 2 Convergence Tickets

EPURE pauses and applies the `needs-human` label (`status: "suspended"`) when human judgment is required:

1. **Sensitive Path Modification**: A `task/*` branch modified `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/agents.yml`, the reviewer roster directory (`<reviewers_dir>/**`, default `.agents/reviewers/**`), or `CODEOWNERS`.
   - *Resolution*: Inspect the diff. If legitimate, add the `approved-sensitive-change` label to the PR and comment **`/epure continue`** (or `/epure approve`) on the tracking issue.
2. **Remediation Cap Reached (`max_code_fix_attempts = 3`)**: A ticket failed Stage 1 tests, external CI, or reviewer `must_fix` checks 3 times in a row.
   - *Resolution*: Push a manual fix commit to the `task/*` or `feature/*` branch (or post a clarifying comment), then comment **`/epure continue`** on the tracking issue. EPURE removes `needs-human`, restores `status: "active"`, skips all already-closed tickets, and resumes from the current milestone.
3. **Zero-Context `EpicConvergenceAudit` & Automatic Phase 2 Tickets (`max_epic_phases`)**:
   - After all Phase 1 tickets are squashed into `feature/*`, EPURE runs a zero-context **`EpicConvergenceAudit`** (`runEpicConvergenceAudit`) against the specification's `EpicGoalContract`.
   - If the audit finds unwired `required_entrypoints` or lingering `forbidden_stubs` (`verdict: "INCOMPLETE"`) and `epic_phase < max_epic_phases` (default `2`), EPURE automatically creates, links, and executes bounded **`[Phase 2 - Ticket N]`** convergence tickets before opening the final `feature/* -> dev` PR. If gaps still remain after `max_epic_phases`, EPURE escalates to `needs-human` (`epic_convergence_exhausted`), where you can push a fix and comment **`/epure continue`**.
4. **Missing Model Configuration or Invalid `.github/agents.yml`**: A command that calls an LLM found neither the action `model` input nor one of `models.planning`, `models.implementation`, or `models.review` (`model_config_missing`, the comment names the missing keys), or `.github/agents.yml` on `dev` fails to parse (`internal_error`, the comment quotes the parser message). EPURE has no fallback model.
   - *Resolution*: Fix or complete `.github/agents.yml` on `dev` (or re-run `setup-repo`, which fills in missing `models.*` keys), then re-post the original `/epure` command; `/epure continue` only resumes implementation-phase runs.

---
## [EN] How-To: Customize Reviewers & Impeccable Gate
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-customize-reviewers

# How-To: Customize the Multi-Agent Reviewer Roster & Impeccable Gate

When you invoke the **`/setup-repo`** skill (and subsequently during `/epure plan`), EPURE dynamically composes and adapts the reviewer roster in the reviewer roster directory (`reviewers_dir` in `.github/agents.yml`, default `.agents/reviewers/*.md`, configurable via `setup-repo --reviewers-dir <path>`) along with the **[Impeccable (`pbakaus/impeccable`)](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** UI quality gate (`DESIGN.md` + `impeccable-gate`), building on the specification and review workflows from **[Matt Pocock's `mattpocock/skills`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)**. This guide explains how the roster is assembled for your project and how to tailor it while preserving prompt-injection immunity.

---

## 1. Always-On Core vs. Dynamic Specialists in `reviewers_dir`

The roster generated by `/setup-repo` is not static: it combines an **always-on cross-cutting core** with **conditional specialists** tailored to your stack and sub-domains (such as the 10-agent example generated for the `craft-calculator` React web app, or custom specialists added via `--domain-reviewers realtime,game-systems` and `--no-frontend-reviewers` for headless repositories):

| Reviewer File | Category | Generation & Selection Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `architecture-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting | Checks deep module boundaries, ADR compliance, and `GLOSSARY.md` ubiquity. |
| `security-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting | Audits secret hygiene, injection surfaces, and privilege boundaries. |
| `spec-parity-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting | Runs on **every** PR (`task/* -> feature/*` and `feature/* -> dev`) to verify 1-to-1 parity with the approved spec. |
| `standards-reviewer.md` | Always-On Cross-Cutting (Stack-Aware) | Adapted to the detected stack (TypeScript `it.each`, Python `pytest.mark.parametrize`, Rust, or Go). |
| `user-advocate.md` | Always-On Persona Gate | Operates in **`design-gate`** mode (on `plan/*` before `/epure approve`) and **`implementation-review`** mode (on PRs). |
| `domain-backend-reviewer.md` (`+ <domain>-reviewer.md`) | Dynamic Domain Specialist | Tailored to the repo's domain (and extendable via `--domain-reviewers <slug>`); selected when domain logic or APIs change. |
| `infra-reviewer.md` | Dynamic Infra Specialist | Selected when CI workflows, build scripts, or dependency manifests change. |
| `frontend-reviewer.md` | Conditional UI Specialist | Generated when the repo includes a UI; selected when `.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, or client state hooks are modified. |
| `accessibility-reviewer.md` | Conditional UI / Impeccable | Generated when the repo includes a UI; audits WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, and `:focus-visible`. |
| `design-reviewer.md` | Conditional UI / Impeccable | Generated when the repo includes a UI; verifies adherence to `DESIGN.md` tokens, responsive layout, and interaction states. |

---

## 2. How the Agent Creates & Customizes Reviewer Prompts Safely

Because the reviewer roster directory (`<reviewers_dir>/**`, default `.agents/reviewers/**`) is a **trusted sensitive path** (Q92):

1. **Tailored Reviewer Creation during `/setup-repo` (and manual additions on `dev`)**: During initial setup, the agent inspects your codebase and can design new specialist files in `<reviewers_dir>/<slug>-reviewer.md` with a `paths:` attribute in the YAML frontmatter (e.g., `paths: src/realtime, src/ws`). Whenever a PR touches a file matching `paths:` (or `<slug>`), `selectReviewersForDiff` automatically selects that specialist.
2. **Always commit changes to `dev`**: At runtime, the EPURE orchestrator loads `<reviewers_dir>/*.md` exclusively from the trusted `dev` branch (falling back to EPURE's embedded templates)—never from an unmerged `task/*` branch.
3. **Automatic Domain Enrichment during `/epure plan`**: When `/epure plan` runs on a new feature, EPURE enriches the domain reviewers and `<reviewers_dir>/user-advocate.md` on the `plan/<issue>-<slug>` branch with new domain invariants and personas. When you run `/epure approve`, those updates merge into `dev` before any `task/*` ticket starts.

---

## 3. Dogfooding & Customizing `DESIGN.md` (Impeccable Gate)

Whenever a repository or PR includes frontend files (`.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.css`, `.html`), the **`impeccable-gate`** check (`evaluateImpeccableFrontendPr`) validates the diff against `DESIGN.md`.

### Blocking vs. Non-Blocking Findings

`impeccable-gate` blocks a PR **only** on objective, verifiable violations:

- **Accessibility (`accessibility`)**: Missing `title` on `<iframe>`, missing `aria-label` on icon/action buttons, missing `:focus-visible` keyboard focus styles, or WCAG 2.1 AA contrast below `4.5:1`.
- **Layout & Responsive (`layout_overflow`)**: Unbounded horizontal overflow or broken mobile viewports (`320px`–`1440px`).
- **Design Tokens (`design_tokens`)**: Hardcoded arbitrary colors bypassing the CSS custom properties declared in `DESIGN.md`.
- **Interaction States (`interaction_states`)**: Interactive async components missing explicit `loading`, `ready`, or `error` states.

Subjective stylistic preferences never block a PR.

---
## [EN] How-To: Promote a Release (dev -> main)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/guides/how-to-release

# How-To: Promote a Release (`dev -> main`)

In EPURE, `dev` is the active default integration branch and `main` is the **immutable release line** protected by the `epure-release-immutability` ruleset. Neither developers nor the `Agent App` can push directly to `main`.

Promoting a release is the **4th Mandatory Human Validation Gate** (Q101).

---

## 1. Prerequisites Before Promoting

Before triggering a release promotion, verify that:

1. All target `feature/* -> dev` Pull Requests have been squash-merged into `dev`.
2. The `CI` workflow on the latest `dev` commit is green.
3. The repository secrets `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are configured, and `<owner>-epure-release` is listed as the Bypass Actor on `epure-release-immutability`.

---

## 2. Trigger the Release Promotion Workflow

You can trigger the release either from the GitHub web UI (**Actions** -> **Release Promote (dev -> main)** -> **Run workflow**) or via the `gh` CLI:

```bash
gh workflow run release-promote.yml \
  -R my-org/craft-calculator \
  -f version=v1.0.0
```

---

## 3. What `release-promote.yml` Executes

1. **Mints a Short-Lived Release App Token**: Signs an RS256 JWT using `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` and `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` to obtain a short-lived installation token for `<owner>-epure-release`.
2. **Verifies Fast-Forward Ancestry**: Checks that `main` is a strict ancestor of `dev` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main origin/dev`). If `main` has diverged, the workflow aborts immediately without forcing a push.
3. **Atomic Fast-Forward & Tag**:
   - Pushes `dev` to `refs/heads/main` (`git push origin dev:refs/heads/main`).
   - Creates and pushes the annotated tag `v1.0.0` pointing to the exact promoted SHA.
   - Publishes the GitHub Release notes generated from the Conventional Commits merged since the previous tag.
4. **Revokes the Ephemeral Token**: Immediately revokes the installation token in an `always()` cleanup step.

---
## [EN] Domain Glossary (EN / FR)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/reference/glossary

# Domain Glossary (English / French Ubiquitous Language)

In accordance with **Q102**, the root `/GLOSSARY.md` file is the single canonical source of truth for EPURE's domain model (rendered natively in the [French Glossary](/fr/reference/glossary)).

This page provides the aligned **English <-> French** ubiquitous language reference table across all architectural rounds (Q1–Q103).

---

## 1. Workflow Step Taxonomy (Q101)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mandatory Human Validation Gates (4)** | *Portes de validation humaine obligatoires (4 jalons)* | The 4 decision points that require an explicit action from a `write+` human contributor and can never be delegated to an agent: (1) `/epure plan` & Grill replies, (2) `/epure approve` locking `spec_sha`, (3) Human squash-merge of `feature/* -> dev`, and (4) Human `workflow_dispatch` of `release-promote.yml`. |
| **Mandatory Automated Steps** | *Étapes automatisées obligatoires* | Deterministic pipeline executed on every approved feature: `plan/*` artifact & ticket DAG generation, secretless TDD loop on `task/*`, multi-agent review from `dev` + AI semantic squash (`task/* -> feature/*`), and synthesis review on `feature/* -> dev`. |
| **Optional or Conditional Steps** | *Étapes facultatives ou conditionnelles* | Steps triggered either conditionally by the change surface (`DESIGN.md` + `user-advocate` + `impeccable-gate` when UI files exist; `needs-human` escalation on sensitive paths or `>3` fix attempts) or optionally by human command (`/prototype`, isolated Pages preview, `/epure to-spec`, `/epure to-tickets`, `/epure status`, `/epure cancel`). |

---

## 2. Core Orchestration & Branch Topology (Q1–Q85)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tracking Issue (Orchestration Issue)** | *Issue de pilotage* | The GitHub Issue where `/epure plan` is invoked, hosting the Grill conversation, the status dashboard, and the `/epure approve` mandate. |
| **Plan Branch (`plan/<issue>-<slug>`)** | *Branche de plan (`plan/*`)* | Documentation-only branch holding `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` before `/epure approve` merges it into `dev`. |
| **Feature Integration Branch (`feature/<issue>-<slug>`)** | *Branche d'intégration de fonctionnalité (`feature/*`)* | Branch created from `dev` upon `/epure approve` that receives autonomous squash-merges from `task/*` PRs before the final human merge into `dev`. |
| **Atomic Task Branch (`task/<ticket>-<slug>`)** | *Branche de tâche (`task/*`)* | Short-lived branch implementing a single ticket from the DAG in a secretless TDD sandbox. |
| **Out-of-Branch CAS State Ref (`refs/epure/state/<issue>`)** | *Référence Git d'état d'orchestration (`refs/epure/state/<issue-number>`)* | Dedicated Git reference outside `refs/heads/*` storing the state machine (`last_processed_comment_id`, signed `spec_sha`, retry counters) updated via atomic Compare-And-Swap. |
| **Batch Comment Cursor (`last_processed_comment_id`)** | *Traitement en lot des commentaires avec curseur* | Mechanism reading all unprocessed human comments in chronological order so queued runs never drop events. |
| **Implicit Grill & Spec Revision Continuity** | *Continuité implicite de l'entretien de grill et de la révision de spécification (Q84)* | Automatic processing of any ordinary human comment posted while the issue is in phase `grilling` (Grill answers) or `spec` (specification revision on `plan/*`), without repeating a slash command. |
| **Human Grill Frontier Validation** | *Validation humaine de la frontière de Grill (Q85)* | Pause in `grilling` (`awaiting_human_approval`) with a Settled Decisions Summary once `frontier_resolved: true`, requiring explicit `/epure to-spec` before generating specification files. |
| **Human Specification Validation** | *Validation humaine de la spécification (Q85)* | Separation between `/epure to-spec` (committing `GLOSSARY.md`, ADRs, `DESIGN.md`, and `docs/specs/<slug>.md` on `plan/*` in phase `spec` / `awaiting_human_approval`) and `/epure to-tickets` (generating the acyclic GitHub Issue DAG in phase `tickets` / `awaiting_human_approval`). |

---

## 3. Security, Governance & Multi-Agent Review (Q86–Q103)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Secretless Sandbox & LLM Proxy** | *Proxy LLM de sandbox* | Isolation boundary stripping `LLM_API_KEY` and GitHub App private keys from consumer test/build subprocesses; fails closed if isolation is unavailable. |
| **Three Governance Rulesets (`epure-feature-governance`, `epure-dev-governance`, `epure-release-immutability`)** | *Séparation des trois Rulesets de gouvernance* | Three distinct GitHub Repository Rulesets: `Agent App` bypasses PRs only on `feature/*`; `dev` requires human merge (`0` review approvals by default for solo maintainer compatibility); `main` and `v*` allow only `Release App`. |
| **Trusted `dev` Reviewer Roster (`reviewers_dir`)** | *Roster de reviewers spécialisés et transverses* | Read-only reviewer definitions (`<name>.md`) initialized by `setup-repo` in the configurable reviewer roster directory (`reviewers_dir`, default `.agents/reviewers/`), always loaded at runtime from `dev` (never from `task/*`), capped at 4 specialists per diff + `spec-parity-reviewer`. |
| **Persona UX Gate (`user-advocate`)** | *Porte UX orientée personas (`user-advocate`)* | Specialist evaluating end-user journeys in `design-gate` mode (enriching ticket acceptance criteria before `/epure approve`) and `implementation-review` mode (blocking PR check on UI changes). |
| **Blocking Design Violation (`impeccable-gate`)** | *Violation de design bloquante* | Objective new UI regression (WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, layout overflow, missing `DESIGN.md` tokens, or missing `loading`/`ready`/`error` interaction states) that blocks PR merge. |
| **AI Semantic Squash Synthesis** | *Synthèse de message de squash sémantique par IA* | Zero-temperature generation of a Conventional Commit title and body right before squash-merge (`Refs #<ticket>` on `feature/*`, `Closes #<issue>` on `dev`). |

---

## 4. Multi-Provider LLM Router & Structured Output (ADR-0029)

| English Term | French Canonical Term (`GLOSSARY.md`) | Definition & Invariant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Multi-Provider LLM Router (`LLMClient`)** | *Routeur LLM multi-fournisseurs* | Dependency-free TypeScript HTTP client routing `<provider>/<model>` identifiers (`openai/`, `azure/`, `azure_ai/`, `google/`, `gemini/`, `anthropic/`, or named aliases in `.github/agents.yml` with lazy `os.environ/VAR_NAME` resolution) without cross-provider fallback on auth/quota errors (ADR-0012). |
| **Schema-Enforced Structured Output (`ResponseSchemaSpec<T>`)** | *Sortie structurée par schéma* | Contract pairing a strict JSON Schema (`responseSchema`, `response_format.json_schema`, or `output_config.format`) with a runtime TypeScript validator, executing a 2-phase tool loop + schema-locked final turn on Google Gemini. |
| **Contextual `/epure` Command Cheat-Sheet (`formatEpureCommandsSpoiler`)** | *Aide-mémoire contextuel des commandes `/epure`* | Collapsible `<details>` block appended to every EPURE issue comment, sub-issue body, and PR description summarizing available commands and highlighting the recommended next action for the current phase. |

## [FR] Introduction & Nom (L'Épure)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/fr/introduction

# Introduction & Sens du Nom EPURE

**EPURE** (`Giskard-AI/epure`) est un framework d'ingénierie logicielle centré sur GitHub qui associe **une gouvernance architecturale humaine structurée** à **une implémentation TDD et une revue de code multi-agents autonomes**.

**EPURE** garantit à l'ingénierie assistée par IA un verrouillage cryptographique du mandat de spécification (`spec_sha`), un fichier de configuration déclaratif unique (`.github/agents.yml`) et un flux reproductible de l'issue jusqu'à la release.

---

## Pourquoi le nom « EPURE » ?

Le nom **EPURE** possède un double sens qui ancre le projet à la fois dans la tradition architecturale française et dans l'ingénierie logicielle moderne :

### 1. L'Épure d'Architecte (Le Tracé Avant l'Usinage)

En architecture classique, en taille de pierre (*stéréotomie*) et en charpente navale, **une épure** est le dessin géométrique tracé à l'échelle grandeur nature sur le mur ou le sol de l'atelier avant même de tailler la première pierre ou d'assembler la moindre pièce.

Dans le développement logiciel assisté par agents IA, la cause principale d'échec est **le codage prématuré** : laisser un modèle deviner les besoins produit, inventer son propre vocabulaire métier ou trancher silencieusement des compromis d'architecture au milieu d'une Pull Request. EPURE impose la discipline inverse :

1. **Tracer l'épure d'abord** : sur une issue GitHub de pilotage, le mainteneur humain et l'agent lèvent chaque ambiguïté lors d'un entretien contradictoire structuré (**le Grill**).
2. **Versionner le domaine et la spécification** : avant qu'une seule ligne de code applicatif ne soit écrite, EPURE versionne le langage ubiquitaire (`GLOSSARY.md`), les décisions d'architecture (`docs/adr/`), la spécification fonctionnelle et technique (`docs/specs/<slug>.md`) et — dès qu'une interface utilisateur est concernée — le contrat de système de design (`DESIGN.md`) sur une branche dédiée `plan/<issue>-<slug>`.
3. **Usiner les pièces sous mandat verrouillé** : ce n'est qu'après la signature explicite du plan par un mainteneur via `/epure approve` (qui verrouille le `spec_sha` exact dans `refs/epure/state/<issue>`) que les agents exécutent le graphe orienté acyclique (DAG) de tickets (`task/* -> feature/*`).

### 2. Le Rétro-Acronyme Bilingue

**EPURE** résume également les cinq piliers de son moteur d'orchestration en français comme en anglais :

| Lettre | Acronyme Français | Acronyme Anglais | Rôle dans le cycle d'ingénierie |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E** | **Élaboration** | **Engineered** | Entretien de conception structuré (`/epure plan` & Grill) qui explicite les compromis avant de coder. |
| **P** | **Plans** | **Planning** | Versionnement de `GLOSSARY.md`, des ADRs, de `DESIGN.md`, de la Spécification et du DAG de tickets (`blocked_by`). |
| **U** | **Usinage** | **Unified** | Boucle d'implémentation TDD en sandbox sans secret (`npm test`, `npm run build`, contrats) sur des branches `task/*` isolées. |
| **R** | **Revue** | **Review** | Revue de code multi-agents spécialisés chargés depuis `dev`, porte UI Impeccable WCAG AA et squash sémantique par IA. |
| **E** | **Exécution** | **Execution** | Intégration gouvernée (merge humain `feature/* -> dev`) et promotion de release fast-forward (`dev -> main`). |

---

## La Tripartition des Étapes du Flux (Q101)

Un principe fondateur d'EPURE est la clarté absolue sur **qui décide** et **ce qui s'exécute automatiquement**. Chaque étape du cycle de vie appartient à l'une des trois catégories formelles suivantes :

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-issue-flow"
  locale="fr"
  title="Flux Global d'une Issue & PR EPURE (Portes Humaines, Obligatoire & Conditionnel)"
  caption="Le flux complet d'EPURE réparti entre les 4 Portes Humaines Obligatoires, le Pipeline Automatisé Obligatoire, la Porte UI Conditionnelle et les Contrôles Facultatifs."
/>

### 1. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--human">Portes de Validation Humaine Obligatoires (4 Jalons)</span>

Aucun agent ne peut contourner ces quatre points de décision. Ils exigent l'intervention explicite d'un contributeur disposant des droits `write` ou `admin` sur le dépôt :

1. **Jalon 1 — Lancement & Réponses au Grill (`/epure plan`)** : un mainteneur déclenche `/epure plan` sur une issue GitHub et répond aux questions de cadrage jusqu'à ce que toutes les ambiguïtés soient levées.
2. **Jalon 2 — Signature du Mandat d'Implémentation (`/epure approve`)** : après relecture de la spécification et du DAG de tickets générés sur `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, le mainteneur poste `/epure approve`. Cette commande intègre directement les artefacts de `plan/*` dans la branche d'intégration `feature/<issue>-<slug>` (avec fusion additive de `GLOSSARY.md` et renumérotation monotone des ADRs, sans PR intermédiaire `plan/* -> dev` selon ADR-0031), scelle le `spec_sha` dans `refs/epure/state/<issue>` et lance l'exécution du DAG de tickets.
3. **Jalon 3 — Merge Humain d'Intégration (`feature/* -> dev`)** : lorsque tous les tickets du DAG sont implémentés, audités et squashés dans `feature/*` (et validés par `EpicConvergenceAudit`), EPURE ouvre la PR finale de synthèse `feature/* -> dev`. Le ruleset `epure-dev-governance` **interdit** matériellement à l'Agent App de fusionner du code applicatif dans `dev` : un humain doit cliquer sur **Squash and merge**.
4. **Jalon 4 — Promotion Humaine de Release (`dev -> main`)** : la promotion de `dev` vers `main` et la publication du tag `vX.Y.Z` exigent le déclenchement manuel (`workflow_dispatch`) du workflow `release-promote.yml` par un mainteneur.

### 2. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--auto">Étapes Automatisées Obligatoires</span>

Dès qu'un jalon humain est franchi, l'orchestrateur EPURE exécute de manière déterministe :

- **Génération de l'Épure, Audit Goldfish de la Spec & DAG de Tickets** : exécution de l'audit de spécification Goldfish zéro-contexte (`runGoldfishSpecAudit`), commit de `GLOSSARY.md`, `docs/adr/` et `docs/specs/<slug>.md` (incluant `EpicGoalContract`) sur `plan/<issue>-<slug>`, puis création des issues GitHub atomiques avec leurs relations natives `sub_issues` et `blocked_by` et le label `ready-for-agent`.
- **Boucle TDD en Sandbox Noyau Sans Secret** : pour chaque ticket débloqué, application des mutations incrémentales (`write_repo_file`, `patch_repo_file`, `delete_repo_file`) et vérification Stage 1 dans une sandbox noyau Linux en 2 phases (`landrun` / `bubblewrap`) dépourvue de `LLM_API_KEY` et des clés privées PEM des GitHub Apps.
- **CI Externe Événementielle, Revue Multi-Agents depuis `dev` & Squash Sémantique IA** : libération immédiate du runner pendant la CI externe (`waiting_ticket_ci`), réveil sur `check_suite.completed` / `workflow_run.completed`, exécution parallèle de jusqu'à 4 reviewers spécialisés (chargés exclusivement depuis `dev`) + `spec-parity-reviewer`, puis synthèse d'un titre/corps Conventional Commit (`Refs #<ticket>`) et squash-merge automatique `task/* -> feature/*`.
- **Audit de Convergence Zéro-Contexte (`EpicConvergenceAudit`) & Revue de Synthèse Finale** : exécution de `runEpicConvergenceAudit` sur `feature/*` pour vérifier le câblage effectif des `required_entrypoints` et l'absence de `forbidden_stubs` (avec création automatique de tickets de Phase 2 si nécessaire), puis ouverture et audit complet de la PR finale `feature/* -> dev` avec les liens `Closes #<issue>` et `Closes #<ticket>`.

### 3. <span class="epure-badge epure-badge--optional">Étapes Facultatives ou Conditionnelles</span>

Ces opérations ne s'activent que selon la nature du changement ou sur demande explicite d'un mainteneur :

- **Porte Conditionnelle UI & Impeccable (automatique si surface UI)** : dès que la fonctionnalité ou le diff touche des fichiers d'interface (`.vue`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.css`, `.html`), EPURE génère automatiquement `DESIGN.md`, exécute `user-advocate` en mode `design-gate` avant `/epure approve`, puis impose `user-advocate` (`implementation-review`) et `impeccable-gate` comme checks bloquants sur chaque PR. Les projets ou tickets purement backend/CLI ignorent automatiquement cette étape.
- **Détour Exploratoire `/prototype` & Preview Pages Isolée (facultatif)** : lorsqu'un comportement visuel ou une machine d'état ne peut être tranché par le texte pendant le Grill, un mainteneur peut demander un prototype jetable sur `prototype/*`. La prévisualisation statique GitHub Pages est **désactivée par défaut** (`enable_pages_preview: false`) et nécessite un consentement explicite.
- **Commandes Slash de Pilotage Granulaire (facultatives)** :
  - `/epure to-spec` : valide la frontière du Grill (ou force le passage anticipé) pour générer la spécification sur `plan/*`.
  - `/epure to-tickets` : valide la spécification sur `plan/*` et génère le DAG natif de tickets GitHub (`sub_issues` + `blocked_by`).
  - `/epure continue` : reprend l'orchestration après une pause `needs-human`, un correctif manuel ou la fin d'une CI externe (`waiting_ticket_ci` / `waiting_feature_ci`).
  - `/epure sync` (alias `/epure rebase`) : synchronise `dev -> feature/*` (et `feature/* -> task/*`) avec résolution de conflits 3-way et validation Sandbox Stage 1.
  - `/epure status` : rafraîchit et affiche l'état d'orchestration et la table d'avancement des tickets.
  - `/epure cancel` (alias `/epure stop`) : interrompt immédiatement l'orchestration et marque le mandat `cancelled` dans `refs/epure/state/<issue>`.
- **Escalade Humaine Conditionnelle (`needs-human`)** : déclenchée automatiquement si une branche `task/*` modifie un chemin sensible (`.github/workflows/**`, `.github/agents.yml`, le répertoire du roster de reviewers `reviewers_dir/**` (par défaut `.agents/reviewers/**`), `CODEOWNERS`) sans exception approuvée, ou si un ticket échoue encore après `max_code_fix_attempts = 3` tours d'auto-remédiation.

---

## Écosystème Amont & Crédits (ADR-0018)

EPURE s'appuie sur des dépôts open source, des skills d'agents, des outils de design et des moteurs de sécurité épinglés par révision (attributions complètes dans [`NOTICE`](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/epure/blob/dev/NOTICE) et [`skills-lock.json`](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/epure/blob/dev/skills-lock.json)) :

| Dépôt Amont | Licence | Rôle dans EPURE |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **[Matt Pocock Agent Skills (`mattpocock/skills`)](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills)** | MIT | Socle des skills de cadrage et d'exécution (`grill-with-docs`, `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `domain-modeling`, `tdd`, `code-review`, `prototype`, `wizard`, `pr` avec crédit à [Dex Horthy / HumanLayer](https://github.com/humanlayer/humanlayer)). |
| **[Impeccable (`pbakaus/impeccable`)](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable)** | Apache-2.0 | Cadrage UX/UI (`shape`, `DESIGN.md`, `.impeccable/surfaces/*.md`) et contrôle qualité déterministe frontend / accessibilité WCAG 2.1 AA (`actions/impeccable`, `impeccable-gate`). |
| **[Archify (`tt-a1i/archify`)](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** | MIT | Moteur de schémas d'architecture interactifs en qualité showcase embarqué dans `scripts/archify/` (`npm run docs:diagrams`). |
| **[iFixAi (`ifixai-ai/iFixAi`)](https://github.com/ifixai-ai/iFixAi)** | Apache-2.0 | Audit déterministe des trajectoires d'autorisation et des frontières de privilèges (`actions/ifixai`). |
| **[zizmor (`woodruffw/zizmor`)](https://github.com/woodruffw/zizmor)** | MIT | Analyse statique de sécurité des workflows GitHub Actions (`actions/zizmor-audit`). |
| **[Renovate (`renovatebot/renovate`)](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate)** | AGPL-3.0 (Outil) | Mise à jour automatisée des workflows épinglés par SHA et des dépendances avec migration assistée optionnelle (`auto_migrate`). |

## [FR] Installation & Skill /setup-repo
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/fr/installation

# Installation & Bootstrap

La façon recommandée d'initialiser ou de reconfigurer un dépôt avec EPURE est d'invoquer le **skill d'agent `/setup-repo`** (`.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`) directement depuis votre agent de développement compatible Skills.

Le skill `/setup-repo` orchestre l'ensemble du bootstrap de bout en bout : il analyse l'architecture réelle de votre dépôt, vous guide avec l'assistant interactif (`setup-github-apps-wizard.sh`) pour enregistrer vos deux GitHub Apps et vos environnements GitHub isolés (`<llm-env>` et `release`), exécute la CLI déterministe (`dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs`) en mode simulation (`--dry-run`) puis application (`--apply`), et **conçoit sur mesure votre roster de reviewers multi-agents (`reviewers_dir`, par défaut `.agents/reviewers/*.md`)**.

---

## Prérequis Système

Avant d'initialiser un dépôt avec EPURE, vérifiez que votre poste dispose de :

- **Un agent compatible Skills** (tout agent IDE ou CLI capable de charger le skill `.agents/skills/setup-repo/SKILL.md`)
- **Node.js 24 LTS** (`>=24.0.0`)
- **GitHub CLI (`gh`)** authentifiée sur votre compte ou organisation cible (`gh auth status`)
- **Git** (`>=2.38`)
- **Une clé API LLM** (`LLM_API_KEY` ou variable fournisseur configurée dans `.github/agents.yml`)

---

## Voie Recommandée : Bootstrapper via le Skill `/setup-repo`

Ouvrez votre dépôt cible dans votre agent et invoquez simplement le skill **`/setup-repo`** :

```text
/setup-repo my-org/craft-calculator
```

L'agent exécute alors un flux guidé en **4 étapes** avec confirmation humaine à chaque opération sensible :

### Étape 1 : Inspection de l'Architecture & des Sous-Domaines par l'Agent

Avant d'écrire le moindre fichier, l'agent inspecte le dépôt cible (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`, arborescence `src/`, présence d'une interface utilisateur, `GLOSSARY.md` existant) afin de déterminer :

- La stack technique pour générer la CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), `verification.targets`, `renovate.json`, `.github/zizmor.yml` et le reviewer de standards (`standards-reviewer.md`).
- La présence ou non d'une surface UI/Frontend (qui conditionne l'activation de la porte **Impeccable** et des reviewers `frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer` et `design-reviewer`).
- Les sous-systèmes métier nécessitant la création de **reviewers spécialisés dédiés** dans `.agents/reviewers/<domaine>-reviewer.md` (ou votre `reviewers_dir` configuré).

### Étape 2 : Provisionnement des Deux GitHub Apps & des Secrets Cloisonnés par Environnement (Wizard)

Pour garantir une séparation stricte des privilèges (Q82, Q91) et zéro exposition de secrets aux workflows publics de Pull Request (conformité Zizmor), EPURE n'utilise jamais de jeton personnel (PAT) omnipotent ni de secrets globaux du dépôt. Chaque dépôt utilise **deux GitHub Apps distinctes** et **deux environnements GitHub isolés** (`<llm-env>` et `release`) :

1. **Agent App (`<owner>-epure-agent`)** : utilisée par l'orchestrateur pour l'automatisation quotidienne (`plan/*`, `task/*`, `feature/*`, Issues, PRs et Check Runs). Elle ne figure **jamais** parmi les Bypass Actors de `dev` ou `main`.
2. **Release App (`<owner>-epure-release`)** : utilisée exclusivement par `release-promote.yml` / `release.yml` lorsqu'un humain déclenche une promotion fast-forward de `dev` vers `main`. C'est le **seul Bypass Actor** autorisé sur `main` et les tags `v*`.

Lancez l'assistant interactif, qui propose l'**Approche 2** (flux local GitHub App Manifest en 1 clic) avec repli automatique sur l'**Approche 1** (enregistrement manuel guidé étape par étape) et injecte les secrets dans leurs environnements GitHub dédiés via `gh secret set --env` sans jamais exposer vos clés privées PEM au modèle LLM :

```bash
bash scripts/wizards/setup-github-apps-wizard.sh \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --llm-env <llm-env>
```

> **Environnement `<llm-env>` libre et agnostique du LLM** : le nom de l'environnement d'agent (`<llm-env>`) vaut `epure-agent` par défaut et peut être choisi librement (autres exemples : `llm`, `openai`, `anthropic` ou `gemini` ; passez la même valeur à `setup-repo --llm-env`) et correspond au champ `environment: <llm-env>` du job `orchestrate-command` dans `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`.

| Nom du Secret | Environnement GitHub Cible | Rôle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | `--env <llm-env>` | Clé API utilisée uniquement par le client/proxy LLM (inaccessible à `authorize-command` et absente de la sandbox d'exécution du code). |
| `EPURE_AGENT_APP_ID` | `--env <llm-env>` | Identifiant numérique de l'application `<owner>-epure-agent`. |
| `EPURE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | `--env <llm-env>` | Clé privée PEM de `<owner>-epure-agent` (sert à signer des jetons d'installation éphémères). |
| `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_ID` | `--env release` | Identifiant numérique de l'application `<owner>-epure-release` (associé à l'environnement protégé `release`). |
| `EPURE_RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` | `--env release` | Clé privée PEM de `<owner>-epure-release` (utilisée uniquement par `release.yml` / `release-promote.yml`). |

Vérifiez le cloisonnement des secrets par environnement via `gh` :

```bash
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator --env <llm-env>
gh secret list -R my-org/craft-calculator --env release
```

### Étape 3 : Simulation Non-Destructive (`--dry-run`)

Le skill `/setup-repo` invoque d'abord la CLI sous-jacente en mode `--dry-run` et vous présente le plan complet des fichiers, branches, labels et rulesets avant toute modification :

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /chemin/vers/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --dry-run
```

### Étape 4 : Application (`--apply`) & Conception sur Mesure du Roster de Reviewers

Après votre validation, le skill `/setup-repo` applique la gouvernance via `--apply --apply-github-settings`, puis rédige et adapte les prompts `.agents/reviewers/*.md` (ou ceux du répertoire choisi via `--reviewers-dir`) propres à votre dépôt :

```bash
node dist/cli/setup-repo.mjs \
  --repo my-org/craft-calculator \
  --target-dir /chemin/vers/craft-calculator \
  --agent-app-id 123456 \
  --release-app-id 654321 \
  --apply \
  --apply-github-settings
```

Commitez et poussez ensuite les fichiers générés (`.github/`, `.agents/reviewers/` et `renovate.json`) sur `dev` :

```bash
git add .github/ .agents/reviewers/ renovate.json
git commit -m "chore(epure): bootstrap repository governance and workflows"
git push origin dev
```

---

## Ce que Configure le Skill `/setup-repo`

1. **Topologie des Branches (`main` & `dev`)** :
   - Crée ou vérifie `main` (ligne de release immuable) et `dev` (branche d'intégration active).
   - Définit **`dev` comme branche par défaut** du dépôt afin que toutes les PRs ciblent `dev` et que les mots-clés `Closes #<issue>` ferment automatiquement les issues lors du merge sur `dev`.
2. **Labels Canoniques de Triage** :
   - Crée ou met à jour les 5 labels canoniques (`needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`) ainsi que les labels d'orchestration (`needs-human`, `approved-sensitive-change`).
3. **Configuration Déclarative, Supply-Chain Durcie & Workflows Appelants** :
   - Génère `.github/agents.yml` (schéma canonique plat avec découverte automatique de `verification.targets`), `.github/zizmor.yml` (configuration d'analyse statique de sécurité des workflows) et `renovate.json` (avec quarantaines de 3 à 14 jours).
   - Installe `.github/workflows/epure-issue-command.yml`, `.github/workflows/epure-check.yml`, `.github/workflows/pr-title.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (adapté à la stack détectée) et `.github/workflows/release.yml`, tous épinglés sur le SHA de 40 caractères d'EPURE (`Giskard-AI/epure`).
4. **Roster Dynamique de Reviewers Multi-Agents (`reviewers_dir`, par défaut `.agents/reviewers/*.md`)** :
   - L'agent qui exécute `/setup-repo` **crée, conçoit et ajoute au besoin les fichiers `<reviewers_dir>/<role>-reviewer.md`** en fonction des éléments réels du dépôt (et `/epure plan` les enrichit ensuite à chaque nouvelle fonctionnalité) :
     - **Socle transverse permanent** : `architecture-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, `spec-parity-reviewer`, `standards-reviewer` (adapté au langage détecté : TypeScript, Python, Rust ou Go) et `user-advocate`.
     - **Spécialistes conçus sur mesure selon les éléments du projet** : `domain-backend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer`, tout reviewer métier créé par l'agent pour vos sous-systèmes (ex. `realtime-reviewer.md`, `combat-engine-reviewer.md`, `sql-migration-reviewer.md` avec routage par `paths:` dans le frontmatter YAML), et — uniquement si le projet comporte une UI — les reviewers frontend/Impeccable (`frontend-reviewer`, `accessibility-reviewer`, `design-reviewer`).
     - *Exemple illustratif sur `craft-calculator` (application web TypeScript + React)* : l'agent assemble un roster de 10 reviewers combinant le socle transverse, `domain-backend-reviewer`, `infra-reviewer` et les 3 reviewers UI/Impeccable.
5. **Politique Squash-Only & 3 Repository Rulesets** :
   - Configure le dépôt en **Squash merge exclusif** (`allow_squash_merge: true`, `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`).
   - Installe les 3 Rulesets GitHub :
     - `epure-feature-governance` (`refs/heads/feature/*`) : `Agent App` en bypass PR pour le squash-merge autonome des PRs `task/* -> feature/*`.
     - `epure-dev-governance` (`refs/heads/dev`) : aucun bypass pour l'`Agent App` (`required_approving_review_count: 0` par défaut pour permettre à un mainteneur solo de merger ses PRs ; configurable via `--require-pr-approvals <N>`).
     - `epure-release-immutability` (`refs/heads/main`, `refs/tags/v*`) : `Release App` comme unique Bypass Actor.

---
## [FR] Usage de Base (Étude de Cas : craft-calculator)
URL: https://giskard-ai.github.io/epure/fr/basic-usage

# Usage de Base (Étude de Cas Réelle : `craft-calculator`)

Pour comprendre comment EPURE fonctionne concrètement, ce guide déroule le cycle de vie complet et anonymisé d'une fonctionnalité réelle sur une application web TypeScript/React nommée **`my-org/craft-calculator`** (un calculateur probabiliste et optimiseur de coûts pour un système d'artisanat incrémental).

Nous allons suivre l'**Issue #16** depuis son ouverture initiale en 3 lignes jusqu'à la release de production **`v1.0.0`** sur `main`.

---

## Votre Parcours Utilisateur de Bout en Bout

À chaque étape du cycle de vie d'une issue, EPURE distingue clairement **ce que vous faites**, **ce qui tourne automatiquement en coulisses**, **quand vous devez à nouveau agir** et **comment fonctionnent l'autofix, la résolution de conflits et la reprise** :

<ArchifyDiagram
  slug="epure-user-journey"
  locale="fr"
  title="Parcours Utilisateur EPURE : Mes Actions, En Coulisses, Quand Réagir & Boucles Autofix"
  caption="Vue interactive centrée utilisateur répondant aux 4 questions clés : que faire, ce qui est automatisé, quand intervenir et comment piloter."
/>
